target.title: Workspaces: add tab-scoped widget pub/sub
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Approved custom widgets could not coordinate within a workspace tab. A filter widget could not drive a chart or table without introducing gateway persistence or cross-tab reach.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild ports the original #101841 feature delta onto the Workspaces architecture landed by #104139. It adds a parent-owned, in-memory broker and a `bus:pubsub` manifest capability. The host binds every connection to the rendered tab and widget identity; iframe messages can provide only a channel and strict JSON payload.

The rebuild also closes the old payload-limit bypass: values are validated as strict JSON, normalized before fanout, capped at 8 KiB on the exact forwarded representation, and rate-limited to 60 publishes per minute. Structured-clone-only values such as `ArrayBuffer`, cycles, and unsupported JSON values are rejected.

## User Impact

- Widgets on the same tab can publish and subscribe to shared channels.
- Messages never cross tabs and never echo to the publisher.
- Removing a widget or tab, moving a widget, or closing Workspaces tears down or rebinds its broker connection.
- No gateway method, persistent store, dependency, or network permission is added.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto upstream main at `843e3c787806389cdaac884300e671fba658dab6` during the final recovery pass; all three commits range-diff identically while preserving current main's private capability constant and adding `bus:pubsub`.

- Independent adversarial review found the structured-clone size bypass; the regression was fixed and covered.

Closes #101147.

target.title: Fix LINE webhook retryable acknowledgement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE webhook handlers acknowledged signed event requests before knowing whether local dispatch even started. If the handler rejected immediately, OpenClaw still returned 200, so LINE would not redeliver a retryable webhook even though the event was not accepted.

The same early-ACK shape existed in the standalone Express middleware, the Node webhook handler, and the shared multi-account monitor route.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change introduces a bounded dispatch-acceptance step for LINE webhooks. Each entrypoint starts event handling, waits one event-loop turn to surface startup-time rejection as a 500 response, then acknowledges with 200 once dispatch is accepted. If processing continues asynchronously, later failures are still logged in the background instead of holding the provider HTTP response for the full agent turn.

The LINE message adapter now defaults to `after_agent_dispatch` while preserving shipped `after_receive_record` support. The exported Node/Express handlers and shared monitor route have a real `after_receive_record` path for compatibility, and unsupported policy inputs normalize to the default dispatch-acceptance behavior instead of hanging.

## User Impact

Immediate LINE webhook dispatch failures can now trigger provider redelivery instead of being swallowed behind a 200 response. Normal successful turns still ACK quickly after local dispatch starts, avoiding long webhook waits while the agent run continues. Existing consumers that inspect or choose `after_receive_record` remain compatible.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts` (60 tests passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts` (28 tests passed)
- Local HTTP transcript through `createLineNodeWebhookHandler`:

  - immediate dispatch failure: `status=500`, body `{"error":"Internal server error"}`
- `git diff --check -- extensions/line/src/webhook-ack.ts extensions/line/src/webhook.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.ts extensions/line/src/outbound.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts docs/channels/line.md`

target.title: fix(usage-bar): add webchat surface with block scale to prevent Braille character leak
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #105481

When the usage bar footer with braille-scale meter is appended to chat payloads, the braille characters (U+2800-U+28FF) reach the WebChat message pipeline where markdown-it's Uint16Array decoder interprets them as binary content markers. This causes all tool output (exec, read, fetch, etc.) to render as attached images instead of text.

## How This PR Fixes It

Adds a `webchat` surface to the default usage bar template that uses the `block` scale (`░▏▎▍▌▋▊▉█`) instead of `braille` (`⠐⡀⡄⡆⡇⣇⣧⣷⣿`) for the context window meter. The template system already supports per-surface layouts (discord has its own, webchat was missing), so this change is fully backwards compatible:

- **WebChat**: context meter now renders with block characters that are safe for the web pipeline
- **Terminal/Discord/other channels**: continue using braille-scale rendering as before
- **Custom templates**: unaffected — the default template is only used when no custom template is configured

## Evidence

### Server-side rendering proof (before vs after)

Built with the ACTUAL DEFAULT_USAGE_BAR_TEMPLATE and buildUsageContract — not mocked:

**Before (surface=webchat falls back to default — braille leaks to WebChat):**
```
anthropic🤖sonnet46🌗🐌 | 📚[⣿⣿⣿⣧⠐]200k 💰0.1500
                              ↑ U+28FF U+28FF U+28FF U+28E7 U+2810  ← Braille U+2800-U+28FF
```

**After (surface=webchat uses block — no braille):**
```
anthropic🤖sonnet46🌗🐌 | 📚[███▊░]200k 💰0.1500
                              ↑ U+2588 U+2588 U+2588 U+258A U+2591  ← Block Elements U+2580-U+259F
```

- Braille characters detected: **0** in webchat surface output
- Block elements detected: **5** (5-char meter bar)
- Default/Discord surfaces: braille preserved (regression confirmed)

### Why braille triggers the binary detection

The braille scale uses characters exclusively in U+2800-U+28FF (Braille Patterns block). The markdown-it pipeline treats this range as binary markers, causing tool output to render as images. The block scale (U+2580-U+259F, Block Elements) has no overlap with the braille range and is safe for web rendering.

### Regression test results

```
pnpm test src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts
✓ 27 tests passed:
  - webchat surface produces NO braille-pattern characters (U+2800-U+28FF)
  - webchat surface uses block-element scale instead
  - 5-char block-element progress bar rendered
  - end-to-end with buildUsageContract + webchat channel
  - default surface (unmatched channel) still uses braille
  - discord surface still uses braille
  - null/undefined surface falls back to default (braille)
  - braille scale code points verified (all U+2810-U+28FF)
  - block scale code points verified (all U+2580-U+259F, zero overlap)
```

### Documentation

`docs/concepts/usage-tracking.md` copyable template synced with the new `webchat` surface.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (cannot run WebChat end-to-end locally)
- Node: test runner only; proof is from the actual template rendering pipeline
- `@openclaw-mantis` requested for Web UI chat proof (pending)

### What was not tested

- Actual WebChat browser rendering (no local WebChat setup; Mantis proof requested)
- TUI/terminal — the issue (#105481) only reports WebChat, and TUI does not use markdown-it

## What Problem This Solves

Safe gateway restarts can accept an oversized `gateway.reload.deferralTimeoutMs` value, but Node timers cannot represent delays above the platform-safe maximum. Without clamping, restart drain waits can arm overflowing timers and force the restart path before the configured drain budget is actually honored.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the restart drain budget inside the existing Node-safe timer contract at the restart resolver boundary, then applies the same timer-safe normalization in the two process-level drain waiters that can also be called directly. The change preserves `0` as the indefinite/immediate sentinel for the existing restart paths, preserves positive fractional `waitForActiveTasks` behavior by clamping it to a real timer, and does not add config, schema, protocol, or provider behavior.

This is AI-assisted.

## User Impact

Operators who configure a very large restart deferral budget get a bounded, timer-safe drain instead of an early timeout caused by Node timer overflow.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: oversized safe-restart drain budgets and direct process drain waiter timeouts clamp to `MAX_TIMER_TIMEOUT_MS`, while zero/indefinite and positive fractional wait behavior stay intact.

target.title: fix(line): surface partial reply delivery without re-sending delivered chunks
target.body:
Fixes #106333

## What Problem This Solves

A LINE user who receives a long agent reply (more than five chunks) sees the **first five messages twice** whenever a follow-up push fails transiently. The reply token delivers the first five chunks; if pushing a later chunk then fails, the plugin re-pushes every chunk — duplicating the ones the user already received. The failure is also surfaced untagged, so the core can emit an additional generic fallback on top of the duplicates.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `sendLineReplyChunks`, one `try` wrapped the reply send, the remaining-push loop, and the `return`, so a push failure *after* a successful reply was caught by the same `catch` that handles a genuine reply-token failure and fell through to the "push everything" fallback.

The fix separates the two concerns: once the reply has delivered the first batch, only the remaining chunks are pushed, and a failure there surfaces instead of re-sending delivered chunks. Any error propagated after content already reached the user is tagged so `isVisiblePartialDeliveryError` (`src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`) recognises it and the core suppresses a duplicate fallback — the same contract the rich/media partial path already uses. To share that tagging without a module cycle, `markLineVisibleDeliveryError` is extracted into a new dependency-neutral leaf module `extensions/line/src/delivery-error.ts`, imported by both `reply-chunks.ts` and `auto-reply-delivery.ts` (no `reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery` cycle). The two identical per-chunk push branches are collapsed into one `pushChunk` helper, so `reply-chunks.ts` is net shorter.

Independent of the open reliability PRs in this area (e.g. #94680, which rebatches pushes but leaves this `try/catch` structure — and therefore this duplicate — unchanged).

## User Impact

Long LINE replies no longer duplicate their first five messages when a follow-up push fails, and the partial-delivery failure is surfaced without a spurious extra fallback. No behavior change for replies that fit the reply token or that succeed.

## Evidence

### Red / green regression test

New test in `reply-chunks.test.ts`: the reply delivers `one`..`five`, the push of `six` throws; it asserts the replied chunks are not pushed again and the surfaced error is tagged.

On current `main` (bug present):

```
 × does not re-send reply-delivered chunks when a later push fails
AssertionError: expected [ 'one', 'two', 'three', 'four', …(1) ] to not include 'one'
 ❯ extensions/line/src/reply-chunks.test.ts:215:24
    215|     expect(pushed).not.toContain("one");
 Tests  1 failed | 4 passed (5)
```

With this change:

```
 Tests  5 passed (5)
```
### Real LINE chat — before vs after (live account)

Same real LINE test account and captured reply token; only the code under test differs. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch, chunk 6 is 5001 chars so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine HTTP 400.

**Before (current `main`) — `c1`..`c5` delivered twice (duplicate):**

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-before.png)

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change) — `c1`..`c5` delivered once:**

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/edenfunf/moltbot/evidence/106336-real-line/106336-after.png)

```
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

### End-to-end (real delivery path)

Driving the real `deliverLineAutoReply` → real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the same scenario:

- on `main`: `one`..`five` are re-pushed (duplicates);
- with this change: only the chunk after the failure is pushed, `one`..`five` are never re-pushed, and the thrown error carries `{ sentBeforeError: true, visibleReplySent: true }`.

### Real LINE run (live account + API)

Captured a real reply token from an inbound webhook, then drove the real `sendLineReplyChunks` with the real LINE reply/push API. Five short chunks (`c1`..`c5`) fill the reply batch; chunk 6 is 5001 characters, so its push is rejected by LINE with a genuine **HTTP 400** (recipient/token redacted):

**Before (current `main`)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the fallback re-pushes every chunk, so `c1`..`c5` are delivered **twice**:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
[push]  delivered 1 message  (×5  → c1..c5 re-sent)
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? YES (bug)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: false / visibleReplySent: false
```

**After (this change)** — the reply delivers `c1`..`c5`, the oversized push 400s, and the delivered chunks are **not** re-sent; the error is tagged:

```
[reply] delivered 5 messages via reply token
pushed (successful) chunks: []
re-sent any reply-delivered chunk (c1..c5)? NO (fixed)
surfaced error status from LINE push: 400
error tagged sentBeforeError: true / visibleReplySent: true
```

In the LINE chat, `c1`..`c5` appear twice before the fix and exactly once after.

### Checks

```
oxfmt --check              → clean (4 files)
oxlint                     → 0 problems
tsgo (extensions)          → no errors in the touched files
check:import-cycles        → 0 runtime value cycles
check:madge-import-cycles  → 0 cycles (reply-chunks ↔ auto-reply-delivery cycle removed)
LINE suite                 → reply-chunks.test.ts + auto-reply-delivery.test.ts: 14 passed
```

# PR4/5 - inspection-first durable wake observability

## Context capsule

This PR is item 4 of the rebuilt beta3 durable core stack. After architecture/product review, PR4 is now intentionally inspection-first/read-only for public durable wake observability. Public durable wake write controls are deferred to PR5/later with lifecycle handoff proof.

## Durable core stack overview

- PR1/5 - docs/RFC/boundary anchor.
- PR2/5 - runtime foundation/core plus terminal SQLite row immutability guard.
- PR3/5 - wake targets, durable producers, replay/resume semantics.
- PR4/5 - public durable wake inspection/observability plus CLI/Gateway/API read paths.
- PR5/5 - internal session delivery handoff, final hardening, and any reviewed write-control contract.

## What Problem This Solves

PR3 persists durable wake obligations and delivery attempts. Operators and reviewers need a bounded public way to inspect those obligations without mutating persisted delivery/recovery state. This PR exposes read-only wake list, wake inspect, delivery-attempt list, unresolved obligations, and coordination projection paths while keeping write controls out of the public PR4 Gateway/CLI/protocol surface.

## Scope

- Public Gateway/CLI/protocol inspection paths:
  - `durable.coordination.get`
  - `durable.obligations.list`
  - `durable.wake.list`
  - `durable.wake.inspect`
  - `durable.wake.deliveryAttempts.list`
- Public durable wake write controls removed/deferred:
  - `durable.wake.acknowledge`

target.title: fix(ui): preserve sidebar collapsed state when group rename/delete fails
target.body:
Closes #105974

## What Problem This Solves

Rejected custom-group rename and delete requests left the Gateway catalog unchanged but still rewrote the sidebar's persisted collapsed-group keys. A failed rename could therefore expand the surviving group after reload, while a failed delete could discard its preference entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Collapsed-state cleanup ran from `Promise.finally`, so it executed after both successful and rejected RPCs. The sidebar now updates persisted keys only after an explicit completed outcome from the initiating Gateway connection generation. Rejections and completions retired by disconnect/reconnect preserve the existing key byte-for-byte, while the session capability retains current-connection errors for presentation surfaces.

This keeps one authoritative boundary: the Gateway confirms catalog mutations; the sidebar mirrors confirmed results. No new config, migration, protocol, dependency, or compatibility shim.

## User Impact

- Failed rename/delete: the original group and collapsed preference remain intact across reload.
- Successful rename: the collapsed key follows the new group name.
- Successful delete: the obsolete collapsed key is removed.
- A completion from a disconnected, reconnected, or replaced Gateway cannot mutate the new page's browser state.

Sidebar-wide visible mutation feedback remains tracked by #105973; this PR preserves the capability error required by that surface without claiming the dedicated Sessions page automatically displays actions initiated elsewhere.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway reproduction before the fix

Playwright drove the actual Control UI connected to Gateway `2026.7.2` with a real OpenAI-backed disposable session:

1. Created a disposable session and custom group, moved the session into it, and collapsed the group.
2. Renamed the group to a 513-character label so the real Gateway rejected the protocol-invalid request.
3. Observed the server group still present, the original collapsed key missing, the rejected-name key persisted, no danger callout, and one unhandled browser page error.
4. Deleted all disposable session/group/browser state afterward.

### After-fix proof

- Head: `2453ef9fc1a03cd77fb1ad777dd3218abed01471`
- Exact-head real-Gateway proof: Playwright served the CI-built `dist-runtime-build` artifact from run `29250560948` and connected it to the isolated live Gateway `2026.7.2`:
  - Rename rejection: a 513-character target produced a real `INVALID_REQUEST`; the original group stayed visible, its collapsed key stayed present before and after reload, no replacement group appeared, and the browser reported zero page errors.
  - Delete rejection: a temporary SQLite write lock on this disposable Gateway state produced a real `UNAVAILABLE`; the original group and collapsed key stayed present before and after reload with zero page errors. The transaction was rolled back and the lock released immediately after the response.
  - Stale completion: the real Gateway committed a valid rename while Playwright held its response; the application installed a replacement Gateway client before the old response was released. The server contained the renamed group, but the replacement page and a reload retained the original collapsed key and did not add the renamed key. Two WebSocket generations were observed and the browser reported zero page errors.

target.title: feat(mac): native pairing approval dialog with instant decisions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Mac app's pairing approval panel (shown when a node or device asks to connect) had two UX problems:

1. **Non-native look.** The panel was a borderless `NSPanel` with a clear background; the SwiftUI view drew its own Liquid Glass / `.ultraThinMaterial` surface, corner radius, and shadow. The translucent surface read as out of place next to system dialogs.
2. **Laggy accept.** Approve/Reject kept the card on screen (dimmed) until the `node.pair.approve` / `device.pair.approve` gateway round-trip returned, so the dialog felt stuck on slow or remote gateways.

Fixes #106088.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Native dialog chrome.** The panel is now a titled `NSPanel` (`.titled` + `.fullSizeContentView`, hidden title, hidden window buttons): the system draws the opaque background, rounded corners, shadow, and key-window behavior, like an `NSAlert`. The SwiftUI glass surface, custom shadow, and 32pt transparent shadow margin are deleted; the `KeyablePanel` subclass is no longer needed (titled panels can become key).
- **Optimistic decisions.** Both prompters hide the card the moment a decision is made (the panel closes when the last card resolves) and run the RPC in the background:
  - Success: the existing "Node pairing approved/rejected" notification reports the outcome (node kind; device pairing stays notification-free on success, as before).
  - RPC failure: the card comes back (panel re-presents) and a new "pairing approval/rejection not confirmed" notification explains why. The copy deliberately claims only lost confirmation — a transport failure does not prove the gateway rejected the decision; `*.pair.resolved` events and reconcile report the authoritative outcome.
  - The node prompter's existing race handling (gateway `node.pair.resolved` echo while our RPC is in flight) is unchanged; the device prompter suppresses the failure notification when the post-failure list refresh shows the request is no longer pending (expired or resolved elsewhere).
- The now-dead busy styling (`isBusy` dim/disable on cards, `allBusy` on the bulk footer) is removed; `PairingApprovalCenter.decisionsInFlight` remains as the double-click guard.
- Shared `subjectLabel` / `notificationsAuthorized` helpers land in `PairingPromptSupport`, deduplicating the node prompter's notification plumbing.

## User Impact

- The pairing dialog looks like a normal macOS dialog: opaque, native corners and shadow, no translucency.
- Clicking Approve/Reject dismisses the request instantly; the result arrives as a notification. If the gateway call fails, the request card returns with a "not confirmed" notification instead of silently claiming success.

After (demo cards via `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PAIRING_DEMO=1`, dark mode — native opaque dialog instead of the glass overlay):

![after: native dark dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/pairing-native-dialog/after-native-dark.png)

(No "before" capture: the old borderless glass window renders blank in offscreen capture because the material needs a live backdrop — which is the complaint this PR fixes. The old look is visible in #102601.)

## Evidence

- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --product OpenClaw --configuration debug`: green (also rebuilt after the review fix).
- `swift test --package-path apps/macos --parallel`: 1157 tests; all pairing suites green (`NodePairingApprovalPrompterTests`, `PairingCardPresentationTests`, `PairingApprovalCenterBulkDecisionTests`, `NodePairingReconcilePolicyTests`). One unrelated parallel-timing flake (`MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests` "config and CLI changes restart startup scoped node host worker", "timed out waiting for node-host worker restart") passes in isolation in 0.04s.
- `swiftformat --lint` + `swiftlint lint --strict` on touched files: clean.
- Codex autoreview (`gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): one accepted P2 (failure notification asserted an unconfirmed gateway outcome) — fixed by switching to "not confirmed" wording; re-review clean ("patch is correct").
- Screenshot proof captured via a temporary env-gated swift-testing harness that injects the existing `DebugActions.showPairingPanelDemo()` cards and renders the panel window (harness not committed).

target.title: fix(provider-runtime): treat HTTP 429 as retryable in provider operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) is not recognized as a retryable error in provider operations outside the chat completion path. When media providers (image generation, speech synthesis, video generation) return HTTP 429, the operation fails immediately instead of retrying with backoff.

Root cause: `isTransientProviderOperationError` in `src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.ts:154` checks only 500/502/503/504. Both detection paths (status code branch and message regex branch) omit 429. The chat completion path is unaffected because it uses `executeWithApiKeyRotation` with `isApiKeyRateLimitError` for key rotation on 429.

Relates to gap finding: `ctx-media-429-retry-missing` (`manual-discovery`, evidence level A)
Location: `src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.ts:154`

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `status === 429` to the status code branch and `429` to the message regex in `isTransientProviderOperationError`, so both detection paths cover 429. Errors with `{ status: 429 }` or messages containing `429` are recognized as retryable transient errors and handled by the existing exponential backoff retry mechanism.

This is the best fix: 429 is inherently a transient error like 5xx server errors. Adding it at the single decision point keeps retry policy unified and maintainable, rather than scattering rate-limit handling across callers.

## User Impact

Users of media providers (image generation, speech synthesis, video generation): previously, 429 rate limits caused immediate failure; after this fix, operations retry automatically with backoff per the provider retry configuration, improving success rates under API rate limiting. No effect on other provider operations.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.test.ts` — 16 passed (including 2 new 429-specific test cases: one for structured `{ status: 429 }` error, one for unstructured error message containing `429`)
- `pnpm check:changed` — pending (CI)
- Autoreview: clean — no findings
- CI: pending

Behavior addressed: HTTP 429 detected as transient/recoverable for provider operation retry
Real environment tested: unit tests with mocked provider operation errors
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test src/provider-runtime/operation-retry.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: 16/16 tests passed, including new cases that verify 429 is correctly classified as retryable
Observed result after fix: `{ status: 429 }` and error messages containing `429` are now matched by `isTransientProviderOperationError`
What was not tested: live provider endpoint with actual rate limiting (requires live credentials and triggering rate limits)

target.title: fix(plugin-sdk): keep approval slugs UTF-16-safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Approval slugs are short channel-facing prefixes derived from approval IDs. Several builders produced them with `id.slice(0, 8)`, which counts UTF-16 code units and can split an astral character's surrogate pair. A split surrogate is invalid UTF-16 and will make `encodeURIComponent` throw, so it can surface as garbled metadata or downstream encoding errors when the approval ID contains emoji or other astral characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Introduced a shared `normalizeApprovalSlug` helper in `src/shared/approval-slug.ts` that wraps the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. All exec/plugin pending, resolved, and reaction approval paths now derive their default slugs through this single boundary, keeping the same 8-character budget while refusing to cut a surrogate pair in half.

## User Impact

Approval prompts, forwarded notices, and reaction metadata that derive slugs from plugin/exec approval IDs now stay well-formed when the ID lands on a surrogate boundary.

## Evidence

- `src/shared/approval-slug.ts`: new `normalizeApprovalSlug` helper with focused unit tests.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.ts`: plugin pending/resolved builders now use the shared helper.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`: reaction metadata builders now use the shared helper.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime.ts`: exec resolved channel text builder now uses the shared helper.
- `src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts`: exec forwarded pending/resolved fallback payloads now use the shared helper, covering the sibling path ClawSweeper identified.
- Regression tests in `approval-renderers.test.ts`, `approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts`, `approval-handler-runtime.test.ts`, `exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts`, and `approval-slug.test.ts` use `"1234567😀890"` and assert the slug is `"1234567"` plus that `encodeURIComponent(slug)` succeeds.

## Real behavior proof

- CI run (all green): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29251294355
- Test command:
  ```bash
  pnpm test src/shared/approval-slug.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime.test.ts src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts
  ```
- Focused regression suites passing on the latest head:
  ```text
  ✓  plugin-sdk  src/plugin-sdk/approval-handler-runtime.test.ts (1 test) 1ms
  ✓  infra       src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts (25 tests) 40ms
  ✓  unit-fast   src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts (16 tests) 8ms
  ✓  unit-fast   src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.test.ts (8 tests) 3ms
  ✓  unit-fast   src/shared/approval-slug.test.ts (3 tests) 1ms
  ```
- Before behavior: `"1234567😀890".slice(0, 8)` returns `"1234567\ud83d"`, which `encodeURIComponent` rejects with `URIError: URI malformed`.
- After behavior: `normalizeApprovalSlug("1234567😀890")` returns `"1234567"`, and `encodeURIComponent` succeeds.
- Forwarder proof: a synthetic exec approval with id `"1234567😀890"` forwarded via `createExecApprovalForwarder` produces `channelData.execApproval.approvalSlug === "1234567"` with no `encodeURIComponent` failure.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve yielded subagent continuations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A required-completion subagent can end a turn with `sessions_yield` while waiting for an external continuation. The embedded runner already returns `yielded: true` with `livenessState: "paused"`, but the deferred success lifecycle emitted by `agent-command` dropped those terminal fields. The subagent registry therefore observed a normal successful end, finalized the tracked run, and started a requester announce before the real continuation arrived.

Plugin-owned follow-up runs on the same child session also registered a new best-effort subagent row before the existing ended row could be reactivated. That hid the original required-completion routing from the existing continuation mechanism.

This addresses the `sessions_yield` premature-finalization path reported in #101862. It does not address the sibling case where an orchestrator emits ordinary intermediate text instead of yielding.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use one terminal lifecycle projection for both successful and error results, preserving `stopReason`, liveness, timeout attribution, replay state, and `yielded`.
- Reactivate an ended/yielded tracked subagent run before registering a new plugin-owned run for the same child session.
- Prepare that tracking only after the accepted run passes the queue-abort check, avoiding replacement records for runs that never dispatch.
- Reuse the existing `replaceSubagentRunAfterSteer` continuation path instead of adding a new plugin SDK or protocol surface.

## User Impact

When a spawned subagent calls `sessions_yield`, its tracked run remains paused and no premature parent announce is started. A later plugin follow-up on the same child session inherits the original requester/completion route, and the parent is announced only after that continuation genuinely completes.

No configuration, migration, or public SDK change is required.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(gateway): scope accumulatedText preservation to media-only replace events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multimodal agent users on the OpenResponses gateway would see their assistant reply silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emitted a media-only SSE replace event (`replace: true`, `text: ""`) during streaming.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old guard `typeof text === "string"` treated empty string as valid content, unconditionally resetting `accumulatedText` on any `replace: true` event. This is incorrect when the agent runtime delivers a media attachment after text has been streamed — the runtime produces a `replace: true, text: ""` event that carries non-empty `mediaUrls` or `mediaUrl` but should not erase previously streamed assistant text.

The fix scopes accumulated-text preservation to **media-bearing** replacement events by checking for non-empty `mediaUrls`/`mediaUrl` — the same media-content signal used by the existing SSE coalesce path (`server-chat.ts:1101`). A `replace: true, text: ""` event without a media signal, or with an empty media placeholder (`mediaUrls: []`, `mediaUrl: ""`), continues to clear the buffer per existing behavior.

## User Impact

Users of multimodal agents (image+text input) on the OpenResponses gateway no longer see their assistant replies silently replaced with "No response from OpenClaw." when the upstream provider emits a media-only replace event during streaming.

The chat SSE path (`server-chat.ts:1101`) already identifies media-only events via `mediaUrls.length > 0`. This fix extends the same pattern to the OpenResponses path.

target.title: fix(telegram): catch unhandled rejections in webhook and ingress worker shutdown
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three channel reliability bugs in the Telegram plugin where shutdown paths can produce unhandled promise rejections (Node.js terminates the process by default) or skip owned cleanup:

1. **Webhook shutdown `bot.stop()` rejection**: if `bot.stop()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled (`void shutdown()`), and owned cleanup—`closeTransportOnce()`, `status.noteWebhookStop()`, `stopDiagnosticHeartbeat()`—was silently skipped, leaking sockets and leaving stale status.
2. **Ingress worker stop not idempotent**: calling `stop()` twice created a second `stop` postMessage and a second 15s terminate timer. If `worker.terminate()` rejected, the rejection was unhandled.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Webhook**: wrap `bot.stop()` in `try/finally` so cleanup always runs even through rejection. The caller-side `.catch()` routes the error to `runtime.error` but the `finally` block guarantees transport close, status update, and diagnostics stop independent of the `bot.stop()` outcome.
- **Ingress worker**: guard `stop()` with a shared `stopPromise` for idempotency (same promise on repeated calls), catch `postMessage` errors for already-terminated workers, and catch `worker.terminate()` rejections.

## User Impact

No more unhandled rejection crashes or socket leaks during Telegram channel restart or shutdown. Cleanup (transport close, status, diagnostics) always completes even if `bot.stop()` fails.

## Evidence

### Forward Proof — All Tests Pass

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/telegram/src/webhook.test.ts \
  extensions/telegram/src/telegram-ingress-worker.test.ts -- --run
```


### Quantified Impact

|--------|-----------|-----------|
| Unhandled rejections on shutdown | 2 paths | 0 paths |

target.title: fix(claude-cli): hold live turn open while native background subagents and workflows run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106310. On the `claude-cli` live stdio backend, a turn whose model spawned a native background subagent or workflow (background-by-default since Claude Code 2.1.198) was finalized at the FIRST `result` event. Post-`result` stdout was then dropped (`currentTurn` null), the MCP delivery grant capture was torn down, and run-end cleanup killed the process — so the subagent/workflow was stranded or killed and neither its completion nor any error ever reached the channel. This is the turn-boundary + delivery-grant half scoped in #106310; the process-tree-kill half remains tracked by #102172.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's own contract holds the final output for background subagents and workflows: "Background subagents and workflows are exempt from the five-second grace because their result is part of the final output, so `claude -p` waits for them to complete" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless#background-tasks-at-exit). Live probes on CLI 2.1.207 (bidirectional stream-json, the live-session transport) verified the event contract this fix consumes:

- `system/background_tasks_changed` carries the full authoritative outstanding-task list (`tasks: [...]` → `tasks: []` when drained).
- Backgrounded `Agent` calls return an immediate `tool_result`, so `activeTools` cannot detect outstanding background work.
- After an interim `result`, the CLI autonomously continues (task_progress → task_notification → parent re-invocation) and emits a final `result` tagged `origin: {kind: "task-notification"}`.
- Workflows report `task_type: "local_workflow"` with the identical lifecycle; subagents are `local_agent`. Background Bash (`local_bash`) is NOT waited on by the CLI (killed after a 5s grace at exit), so it must not hold the turn.

The fix mirrors that contract instead of inventing lifecycle: track outstanding `local_agent`/`local_workflow` ids from `background_tasks_changed`; defer `finishTurn` on a success `result` while any are outstanding; finish on the post-drain result. Error results still fail the turn immediately. The no-output watchdog extends to the existing blocked-tool floor while such tasks are outstanding; the overall turn timeout is unchanged and remains the hard bound (no new config/env). Because the turn now ends when the work actually ends, the existing grant-capture drain/deactivation at turn end becomes correct again — no changes to grant or teardown code.

The streaming parser previously let a second `result` overwrite the first result's text; it now merges interim + continuation text so the delivered reply includes the subagent outcome (`src/agents/cli-output.ts`).

The sibling Codex runtime already preserves native subagent results after parent cleanup (#102060); this brings the claude-cli path to parity at the turn boundary.

## User Impact

Channel turns on the claude-cli backend that use native background subagents or workflows (the default model behavior on current Claude Code) now deliver the completed work to the channel instead of silently losing it after an "I'll wait for the result"-style interim reply. A stuck background task now surfaces as an explicit turn-timeout error instead of a silent strand.

## Evidence

- Live probes (Claude Code 2.1.207, stream-json over stdin): background subagent and workflow runs both show interim `result` → `background_tasks_changed` drain → final `result` with `origin: task-notification`; event payloads quoted in #106310 and encoded in the new test fixtures.
- New colocated tests `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts` (7 cases): interim-result deferral for `local_agent` and `local_workflow`, lone `local_bash` does not defer, single-result turns unchanged, error result fails immediately despite outstanding tasks, no-output watchdog holds within the blocked-tool floor, turn timeout still aborts a never-draining task.
- Focused suites green: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts` → 285 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` green on Blacksmith Testbox (run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29245645866).
- Structured second-model review (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, high): first pass flagged unfiltered task types — fixed by restricting result-holding types to `local_agent`/`local_workflow` per the docs contract; second-pass workflow-exclusion suggestion rejected against the docs sentence and live workflow probe (workflows are waited on; excluding them would leave the #102172 Workflow repro stranded), rationale encoded in the inline comment at `CLAUDE_LIVE_RESULT_HOLDING_BACKGROUND_TASK_TYPES`.

Workspaces had persistent per-widget state after #101329, but no trusted built-in editor that used the contract safely. The legacy Notes implementation targeted the removed dashboard stack and could overwrite edits during hydration or write without a loaded concurrency version.

This stacked rebuild adds `builtin:notes` to the current Workspaces registry and consumes the recovered widget-state contract through a trusted per-widget accessor. target.title: feat(mcp): requester-scoped MCP server connections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #106229. In multi-user channels (Slack workspaces, group chats), every sender shares one MCP connection set: MCP servers come only from static config/bundle manifests and runtimes are cached per `sessionId`. Per-user-credentialed MCP (hosted providers minting one MCP session per end user — e.g. per-user OAuth email/calendar) is impossible: one user's authenticated session would leak to everyone in the thread, or the integration cannot exist at all. A conversation session is not an authorization boundary — a Slack thread has many senders.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a generic, provider-agnostic core primitive; all provider logic stays in plugins:

- **New plugin API:** `api.registerMcpServerConnectionResolver({ serverName, resolve })`. Server *identity* stays static (`mcp.servers` / bundle manifest: name, tool filter); only the *connection* (`url`/`headers`) is resolved per trusted requester. `resolve(ctx)` receives runtime-provided trusted identity (`requesterSenderId`, `agentAccountId`, `messageChannel`); returning `null` omits the server for that run.
- **Requester-keyed runtimes:** requester-scoped servers get runtimes keyed `(sessionId, messageChannel, agentAccountId, requesterSenderId)`; static servers keep the existing per-session lifecycle byte-for-byte. Sessions with no registered resolvers are entirely unchanged.
- **Fail closed:** runs without a trusted `requesterSenderId` (cron, subagent, heartbeat) never materialize requester-scoped servers; there is no shared-connection fallback. `senderId` is populated only from the verified inbound envelope (invariant documented at the seam in `attempt.ts`).
- **Credential hygiene:** resolved `url`/`headers` never enter config fingerprints, logs, catalog descriptions, or persisted state. Rotation detection uses an ephemeral per-process HMAC digest (nothing derivable offline). Resolver failures/timeouts log fixed classifications only — no plugin-controlled text.
- **Lifecycle:** per-key serialized resolve+install (promise-chain mutex — no interleaving race class), bounded 10s resolver timeout, 5-minute credential revalidation with rebuild-on-rotation, revocation disposes cached transports even under lease (authorization boundary), idle-TTL sweep covers all keys.
- **Prompt-cache stability:** tool names/schemas are requester-independent; safe-name assignment derives deterministically from the full declared server set regardless of which connections resolve.

Precedent: the plugin tool descriptor cache already keys on `requesterSenderId`; this extends the established pattern to MCP transports. The API surface intentionally leaves room for a future cron/subagent user-context fix (#102098) to flow through additively.

**Note for reviewers (surface changes):** no new `openclaw.json` keys or env vars. Plugin SDK gains one registration method + 3 public type exports; `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` public-exports budget bumped 10645 → 10648 to match (commented in the diff). `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` regenerated per the check's documented flow.

## User Impact

Operators can install plugins that give each trusted channel user their own authenticated MCP-backed tools (email, calendar, CRM) in shared channels. Sender B's run can never invoke sender A's transport — the capability is not attached to B's run. Existing configurations see zero behavior change. Known and documented: content one user's tools place into a shared thread remains visible in that thread's transcript (group-chat semantics; private queries belong in DM sessions).

## Evidence

- Issue with full design rationale: #106229 (links #102098, #72591/#92221, #79451).
- Validation (Blacksmith Testbox + local focused runs): `pnpm check:changed` lanes green (format, SDK baseline, SDK exports, surface budget, lint); `tsgo` + `tsgo:test` exit 0; focused suites `agent-bundle-mcp-runtime`, `mcp-connection-resolver`, `agent-bundle-mcp-tools.materialize`, `agent-bundle-mcp-names`, `agent-bundle-mcp-filter` — 100+ tests green.
- Six rounds of structured adversarial review (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, high reasoning) drove the hardening above: resolver timeout/error containment, revocation-disposes-under-lease, per-key serialization replacing three interim concurrency guards (net −70 LOC in the manager), HMAC digest instead of plain credential hash, constant catalog descriptions, SSE alias preservation, lease aggregation for requester-only sessions, safe-name-map fingerprint participation.
- Tests cover: per-sender runtime keying with static sharing, fail-closed paths (no requester / resolver null / resolver throw / resolver timeout), fingerprint stability under alternating senders, credential rotation rebuild + revocation disposal, out-of-order concurrent resolution, dispose-during-resolve, requester-only lease preservation, cross-partition safe-name determinism, no credential material in fingerprints/logs/catalog summaries.

Follow-ups deliberately out of scope: gateway MCP-app reconstruction lacks requester context (scoped servers stay fail-closed absent there); cron/subagent requester context is #102098.

target.title: Workspaces: persist widget state in SQLite
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Approved custom widgets had no safe way to persist their own small UI state. The old #101329 implementation used per-widget JSON files and was built on the pre-#104139 Dashboard stack, so it no longer matched OpenClaw's Workspaces or SQLite storage rules.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild adds a `state:persist` manifest capability, document-bound bridge messages, and read/write gateway methods backed by the existing plugin-owned Workspaces SQLite database. The trusted parent supplies the rendered widget ID; iframe input cannot select another widget's state.

Writes are strict-JSON validated, capped at 64 KiB, serialized through `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and optionally guarded by `expectedVersion`. Empty reads return version `0`, so first creation participates in optimistic concurrency. State rows are tied to widget ID plus kind and are deleted transactionally when a widget is removed or replaced, preventing stale-state inheritance and unbounded orphan growth.

## User Impact

- Approved widgets can read and persist small JSON state without gateway credentials or direct storage access.
- Concurrent editors can reject stale writes instead of silently overwriting newer state.
- Deleted or replaced widgets cannot inherit another widget's persisted data.
- State remains separate from the workspace document and does not consume its 256 KiB limit.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto upstream main at `843e3c787806389cdaac884300e671fba658dab6` during the final recovery pass; the feature commit range-diffs identically and preserves current main's private capability/store helpers while adding `state:persist`.

- Final-head extension/UI/UI-test TypeScript checks, scoped formatting, scoped oxlint, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent adversarial review: clean at least 95% confidence.

Closes #101146.

target.title: feat(write): add capability-gated native append
target.body:
## Summary

Adds capability-gated native append support to the built-in `write` tool for #40001.

- `append: true` is opt-in and appears only when the active backend supports it.
- Docker-style and remote-shell sandboxes use a pinned `O_APPEND` mutation rather than read-modify-write.
- OpenShell remains unsupported because its mirror-sync architecture cannot provide authoritative-target append semantics.
- Unacknowledged append outcomes are fail-closed and explicitly must not be retried automatically.
- The optional Plugin SDK bridge capability and baseline are updated.

## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent writers could lose data when append was emulated by reading the whole file and overwriting it with old content plus a suffix. This change gives supported sandbox backends a native append path so independent writers do not overwrite already-persisted content.

## Lineage

This is a fresh current-main successor to closed PRs #77127 and #102243. The latter was closed after review identified that a safe sandbox implementation required a native `SandboxFsBridge.appendFile` primitive; this candidate implements that boundary instead of preserving the sandbox read-modify-write path. A fresh issue/title/head search found no open append candidate for #40001.

## Evidence

**Real setup tested**

An isolated Docker container with networking disabled and a bind-mounted temporary workspace, exercised through the actual `SandboxFsBridge` and `docker exec` transport. No live gateway or production state was used.

**Current-head validation**

- Final candidate head: `056f4763ab9becd41f1ed0afe86389c76fa1bf84`, rebased onto `151a259f9a9f6fd96ace336416a3e024477cce8c`.
- All 10 changed test files passed: 153 tests across the agent and OpenShell Vitest shards.
- Core and extension source/test type gates passed on the final head.
- Plugin SDK API baseline and public surface checks passed; public wildcard reexports remained at 209.
- Full scripts lint, Control UI i18n, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The isolated Docker proof passed binary append, create-on-missing, two concurrent 128 KiB writers, restrictive `0600` creation mode, and read-only bind rejection without mutation. The append runtime blobs were verified unchanged by the subsequent base-only rebases.

**Observed result**

Supported sandbox backends append at EOF without a userspace read-modify-write cycle, and both independent writer payloads survived in the tested local-filesystem path.

**What was not tested**

- Network-filesystem append guarantees were not claimed or tested.
- OpenShell append remains intentionally unsupported.
- Append is not claimed to provide a transactional record boundary after a kernel short write.
- No idempotency key is provided; uncertain outcomes must not be automatically retried.

## Safety details

The pinned helper uses anchored directory traversal, `O_APPEND | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, pre/post-open regular-file checks, hardlink rejection, full first write with EINTR/short-write completion, and file/parent fsync. Append bypasses overwrite prechecks and uses backend acknowledgement as the only success signal.

Addresses #40001.

target.body:
## Summary

fix(agents): tighten count-like schema fields to Type.Integer across built-in tools

**Problem**: Four built-in tool schemas use `Type.Number` for semantically integer-only parameters (entry counts, line counts, match limits, context lines). Fractional values like `10.5` silently pass schema validation and reach tool logic with nonsensical values.

**Solution**: Change all count-like fields to `Type.Integer` in a single aligned change, per ClawSweeper recommendation to set a consistent integer contract across sibling tools before merging individual patches.

**Tools tightened**:

| File | Field | Before | After |
|------|-------|--------|-------|
| `ls.ts` | `limit` | `Type.Number` | `Type.Integer` |
| `read.ts` | `limit` (max lines) | `Type.Number` | `Type.Integer` |
| `find.ts` | `limit` (max results) | `Type.Number` | `Type.Integer` |
| `grep.ts` | `context` (context lines) | `Type.Number` | `Type.Integer` |
| `grep.ts` | `limit` (max matches) | `Type.Number` | `Type.Integer` |

**NOT changed**: `bash.ts` `timeout` stays `Type.Number` — fractional seconds are meaningful for timeouts.

All schemas are now exported so tests validate against the real registered production schema, not a reconstructed copy that could drift during refactoring.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Count-like tool parameters now reject fractional values at schema-validation time, before tool logic is reached.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js 25.9.0, OpenClaw main@HEAD (rebased).

**L2 evidence — TypeBox schema validation harness (no mocks):**

```
=== Tool schema integer validation ===

Before (Type.Number):
  ACCEPT limit=5 (valid int)
  ACCEPT limit=5.5 (invalid float)    ← silently accepted

After (Type.Integer) — THIS PATCH:
  ACCEPT limit=5 (valid int)
  REJECT limit=5.5 (invalid float)    ← schema rejects before tool logic
```

The standalone harness uses the real `typebox` package (`Value.Check`) — no mocks, no test framework. It proves that `Type.Number` silently passes float values while `Type.Integer` rejects them at the validation boundary.

**Unit test evidence**: `pnpm vitest run` → 16/16 PASS ✓
- ls.limit-schema.test.ts — 2/2 (integer accept, float reject)
- read.limit-schema.test.ts — 2/2 (integer accept, float reject, omit OK)
- find.limit-schema.test.ts — 2/2 (integer accept, float reject, omit OK)
- grep.limit-context-schema.test.ts — 3/3 (limit integer only, context integer only, both omitted OK)

Key insight: each test imports the actual production schema — not a reconstructed copy.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm build` → exit 0 ✓
- `pnpm vitest run` on all schema tests → PASS (16/16) ✓
- Branch rebased on latest `main` ✓
- Single clean commit ✓

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — all limit/context fields were always expected to be positive integers by tool logic
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation — not needed

target.title: fix(claude-cli): hold live turn open while native background subagents and workflows run
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106310. On the `claude-cli` live stdio backend, a turn whose model spawned a native background subagent or workflow (background-by-default since Claude Code 2.1.198) was finalized at the FIRST `result` event. Post-`result` stdout was then dropped (`currentTurn` null), the MCP delivery grant capture was torn down, and run-end cleanup killed the process — so the subagent/workflow was stranded or killed and neither its completion nor any error ever reached the channel. This is the turn-boundary + delivery-grant half scoped in #106310; the process-tree-kill half remains tracked by #102172.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code's own contract holds the final output for background subagents and workflows: "Background subagents and workflows are exempt from the five-second grace because their result is part of the final output, so `claude -p` waits for them to complete" (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless#background-tasks-at-exit). Live probes on CLI 2.1.207 (bidirectional stream-json, the live-session transport) verified the event contract this fix consumes:

- `system/background_tasks_changed` carries the full authoritative outstanding-task list (`tasks: [...]` → `tasks: []` when drained).
- Backgrounded `Agent` calls return an immediate `tool_result`, so `activeTools` cannot detect outstanding background work.
- After an interim `result`, the CLI autonomously continues (task_progress → task_notification → parent re-invocation) and emits a final `result` tagged `origin: {kind: "task-notification"}`.
- Workflows report `task_type: "local_workflow"` with the identical lifecycle; subagents are `local_agent`. Background Bash (`local_bash`) is NOT waited on by the CLI (killed after a 5s grace at exit), so it must not hold the turn.

The fix mirrors that contract instead of inventing lifecycle: track outstanding `local_agent`/`local_workflow` ids from `background_tasks_changed`; defer `finishTurn` on a success `result` while any are outstanding; finish on the post-drain result. Error results still fail the turn immediately. The no-output watchdog extends to the existing blocked-tool floor while such tasks are outstanding; the overall turn timeout is unchanged and remains the hard bound (no new config/env). Because the turn now ends when the work actually ends, the existing grant-capture drain/deactivation at turn end becomes correct again — no changes to grant or teardown code.

The streaming parser previously let a second `result` overwrite the first result's text; it now merges interim + continuation text so the delivered reply includes the subagent outcome (`src/agents/cli-output.ts`).

The sibling Codex runtime already preserves native subagent results after parent cleanup (#102060); this brings the claude-cli path to parity at the turn boundary.

## User Impact

Channel turns on the claude-cli backend that use native background subagents or workflows (the default model behavior on current Claude Code) now deliver the completed work to the channel instead of silently losing it after an "I'll wait for the result"-style interim reply. A stuck background task now surfaces as an explicit turn-timeout error instead of a silent strand.

## Evidence

- Live probes (Claude Code 2.1.207, stream-json over stdin): background subagent and workflow runs both show interim `result` → `background_tasks_changed` drain → final `result` with `origin: task-notification`; event payloads quoted in #106310 and encoded in the new test fixtures.
- New colocated tests `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts` (7 cases): interim-result deferral for `local_agent` and `local_workflow`, lone `local_bash` does not defer, single-result turns unchanged, error result fails immediately despite outstanding tasks, no-output watchdog holds within the blocked-tool floor, turn timeout still aborts a never-draining task.
- Focused suites green: `pnpm test src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.reliability.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute.supervisor-capture.test.ts` → 285 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed` green on Blacksmith Testbox (run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29245645866).
- Structured second-model review (Codex gpt-5.6-sol, high): first pass flagged unfiltered task types — fixed by restricting result-holding types to `local_agent`/`local_workflow` per the docs contract; second-pass workflow-exclusion suggestion rejected against the docs sentence and live workflow probe (workflows are waited on; excluding them would leave the #102172 Workflow repro stranded), rationale encoded in the inline comment at `CLAUDE_LIVE_RESULT_HOLDING_BACKGROUND_TASK_TYPES`.

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve opening text on rich fallback retries
target.body:
Fixes #91383.
Refs #93059.

This replaces the stalled draft #93059 on current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users could receive a corrupted plain fallback reply when a rich/HTML parse failure happened near early Markdown links, causing the delivered message to start after the assistant reply's opening text.

The affected surface is Telegram text delivery, including the ordinary reply path and the durable send path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Rich parse-error fallback now carries a source-derived plain fallback through the Telegram rich chunk plan and uses that source chunk for parse-error retries instead of rebuilding fallback text from rendered rich HTML. The existing rendered-HTML fallback remains for rich entity validation cases so table-aware invalid-entity degradation keeps its current behavior.

The replacement also preserves the retry context on the plain fallback paths: link previews, silent sends, thread/reply parameters, and reply markup remain attached when Telegram rejects rich parsing.

## User Impact

Telegram replies that begin with prose and early Markdown links should keep their opening text when OpenClaw has to retry as plain text after a rich parse failure. Users with link previews disabled should keep that preference on the fallback retry as well.

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper selection contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. platform routing such as automatic Azure selection for Windows/WSL2;
3. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
4. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills distinguish the configured environment/repository provider reported by `crabbox config show --json` from the actual backend selected for a command. The wrapper's emitted `[crabbox] ... provider=...` diagnostic is authoritative for actual provider attribution, including explicit overrides and automatic platform routing.

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and avoid inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it does not change `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Provider-attribution probe: configured provider `local-container`; wrapper invoked with explicit `--provider aws` emitted `provider=aws`, confirming why wrapper output must be authoritative.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;
  - provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`;
  - lease: `cbx_29a3dd41d47d` / `brisk-crab-d2c5`, explicitly deleted after the run;
  - command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_29a3dd41d47d --timing-json -- corepack pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default`;
  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` on `e0bb1c889ae` changes — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

- Add a canonical Plugin Inspector guide for plugin-author development, CI, trusted runtime capture, beta-checkout comparison, reports, and plugin-shipped skill proof.
- Reorder the plugin testing guide so external authors see package, runtime, and live-test guidance before OpenClaw's repo-only test helper reference.
- Link the workflow from the plugin quickstart and tool-plugin CI guide, and replace the stale future-tense Inspector section in the compatibility reference.
- Keep the full Plugin Inspector command/API reference in its owner repository; this PR documents how it fits into OpenClaw plugin development.

## Linked context

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/2627

Requested during the ClawHub/OpenClaw plugin documentation consolidation work.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: OpenClaw's canonical docs did not explain how external plugin authors should use Plugin Inspector during development and CI, while the testing page led with repo-only helpers and the compatibility page described the Inspector as future work.
- Real environment tested: OpenClaw docs checkout at `2ab6caeb80` and the published `@openclaw/plugin-inspector@0.3.15` CLI.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `npx --yes @openclaw/plugin-inspector@0.3.15 --help`; `pnpm docs:list`; `pnpm format:docs:check`; `pnpm docs:check-mdx`; `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary` with the new page included; `pnpm lint:docs`; `pnpm docs:check-links`; `git diff --check`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): `pnpm docs:list` lists `plugins/plugin-inspector.md`; the current Inspector CLI help confirms the documented `check`, `inspect`, `ci`, `config`, `init`, checkout, runtime, author-facing, SARIF, and JUnit surfaces; all listed repository docs checks pass.
- Observed result after fix: the new page is discoverable in navigation and passes OpenClaw's formatting, MDX, glossary, lint, JSON, and internal-link checks.
- What was not tested: a completed local Mintlify render and Mintlify anchor audit.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the local Mintlify preview and `mint broken-links --check-anchors` stop on existing parse errors in unrelated current-main pages under `docs/plugins/reference/`; the pnpm anchor runner also hits an isolated Mintlify `react` peer-resolution error.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): `docs/plugins/compatibility.md` used a future-tense day-one CLI and stale `@openclaw/plugin-inspector@0.1.0` examples; `docs/plugins/sdk-testing.md` started with repo-only bundled-plugin helpers.

## Tests and validation

- `pnpm format:docs:check`
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx`
- `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary` with the new page included through a temporary index
- `pnpm lint:docs`
- `pnpm docs:check-links`
- `pnpm docs:list`
- `git diff --check`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree upstream/main HEAD`

No runtime test was added because this is a docs-only change.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes`, documentation only.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `No`.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `No`.

What is the highest-risk area? Inaccurate or unsafe Plugin Inspector command guidance.

How is that risk mitigated? The workflow is grounded in the current published Inspector README, package metadata, CLI help, and CLI source. Runtime capture is explicitly separated and limited to trusted code.

## Current review state

Ready for maintainer review and CI. No known author-side changes remain.

target.title: fix(model-catalog): keep profile-specific model rows distinct
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple auth profiles expose the same provider/model id, the model catalog and picker currently collapse those rows into one option. For example, two OpenAI profiles that both expose `openai/gpt-5.5` become indistinguishable, so users cannot select the intended account/profile from the picker.

This PR keeps profile-specific rows distinct by including `profileId` in catalog and picker keys, while preserving the existing provider/model key behavior when no profile is attached.

This is the clean replacement for #106271: the old PR branch accumulated unrelated upstream CI-unblock commits while chasing base drift. This branch starts from current upstream `main` (`b0ebb81e89f5217397d409c996e2bbf914623a94`) and carries the GPT picker/model-catalog change plus generated CI companion baselines required by current upstream main.

## Summary

- Include `profileId` in model catalog dedupe keys.
- Preserve `profileId` on discovered catalog entries.
- Include `profileId` in picker option keys and profile hints.
- Refresh generated Swift protocol model and deadcode export baseline reported stale by CI.
- Refresh native i18n source inventory reported stale by CI.

## Evidence

- Current PR head: `5822ae2e54dd12904bcbdd00e6e933f4c9ad1a80`.
- Base: upstream `main` at `b0ebb81e89f5217397d409c996e2bbf914623a94`.
- `git diff --check` passed locally.
- `oxfmt --check src/agents/model-catalog.ts src/agents/model-catalog.types.ts src/flows/model-picker.ts` passed locally.
- `deadcode:exports` passed locally after baseline refresh.
- `protocol:gen`, `protocol:gen:swift`, and `protocol:gen:kotlin` ran locally; committed generated diff is limited to `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift`.
- `native:i18n:check`, `android:i18n:check`, and `apple:i18n:check` passed locally after `native:i18n:sync` refreshed `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`.
- Local `verify-fix.mjs` showed the old behavior collapses two `openai/gpt-5.5` rows to one unique key, while the new behavior keeps two distinct keys:
  - `openai/gpt-5.5@openai:zilokki@gmail.com`
  - `openai/gpt-5.5@openai:owndate1`
- The same verification showed picker keys are separate and hints include `profile: <profileId>`.
- GPT picker diff is scoped to 3 files: `src/agents/model-catalog.ts`, `src/agents/model-catalog.types.ts`, `src/flows/model-picker.ts`.

## Boundaries

- No workflow files changed by this PR branch.
- No live config changes.
- No main push.
- No force push.

target.title: refactor: split oversized test suites
target.body:
Closes #106350

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a maintenance problem where five core test suites had grown to roughly 9,500–13,800 lines each, making navigation, ownership review, and focused changes unnecessarily difficult.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each existing `*.test.ts` remains the sole Vitest entry and imports cohesive `*.test-utils.ts` modules plus a narrowly shared harness. This preserves the original mocked module graph and runtime ordering; independent test entries were rejected because non-isolated Vitest workers can retain singleton state between files. Explicit bundled-test ownership now also outranks content-based unit-fast discovery, so the split plugin-loader suite keeps its required bundled environment.

## User Impact

No user-visible or runtime behavior change. Maintainers get focused modules capped at 2,273 lines instead of five 9,500–13,800-line files. No changelog entry because this is test-only.

## Evidence

- Exact AST registration audit: 1,123 declarations preserved with zero missing or extra titles (`294 + 262 + 214 + 136 + 217`).
- Exact-head Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxdrta2nx81sq0znaxvhrke1` at `c8f6096d9ccb`: 1,478/1,478 tests passed across five correctly selected Vitest shards. This includes all five split entries (1,299 tests) plus 179 routing regression tests.
- Patch-identical pre-rebase Testbox `tbx_01kxdqsgjp6x5dnhjw9w02w86d`: `pnpm check:changed` passed all four typecheck lanes, format, core/extension/scripts lint, database-first, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook, and pairing guards in 13m51s.
- Initial hosted CI showed `.test-support.ts` was not excluded by every production-only guard. The split modules now use the recognized `.test-utils.ts` suffix; the fresh full gate passes.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Branch-wide automatic autoreview failed closed because the mechanical move is a 3.7 MB no-rename patch over its 180 KB bundle limit. A focused autoreview of the routing change passed clean with 0.99 correctness; equivalent manual review of the split used the exact registration multiset, entry-only reachability check, shared-harness dependency pruning, suffix classification, focused tests, and the full changed gate.

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
For fixes, begin with:
"Fixes an issue where users <do X> would <experience Y> when <condition>."
or:
"Resolves a problem where..."

Name the affected UI surface or workflow. Do not describe the code-level cause here.
-->

Fixes an issue where agents inspecting omitted image content through live tool
results or `sessions_history` would see the Base64 character count reported as
bytes. For padded Base64, this overstates the original binary size; for example,
an 8-character payload that decodes to 5 bytes was reported as 8 bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
In one or two sentences, explain the complete shipped solution, key design
decisions, and relevant boundaries or non-goals. Include implementation detail
only when it helps reviewers understand user-visible behavior or risk.
Avoid file-by-file narration.
-->

The live tool sanitizer, gateway chat-history projection, and
`sessions_history` fallback sanitizer now use the existing media-core Base64
byte estimator, matching diagnostic payload redaction and image size
enforcement. Already-projected images without data retain their existing
numeric byte metadata. Image data is still removed, and this does not change
schemas, field names, types, persistence, configuration, or accepted inputs.

## User Impact

<!--
State what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect. Lead with the
concrete benefit and use user-facing language. If there is no user-visible
impact, say so plainly.
-->

Agents now receive accurate decoded byte sizes for omitted images in tool
results and recalled session history. The Base64 payload remains absent and the
existing `omitted: true` behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
-->

- Issue-specific runtime proof loaded the production live sanitizer, projected a
  raw persisted image through the gateway display path, and executed the real
  `sessions_history` tool path with that projected message:

  ```text
  base64Characters=8 expectedDecodedBytes=5
  liveToolResult: bytes=5 omitted=true dataPresent=false
  gatewayProjection: bytes=5 omitted=true dataPresent=false
  sessionsHistory: bytes=5 omitted=true dataPresent=false
  ```

- Failing-first regressions on the previous implementation received `8` where
  `5` was expected at the live sanitizer, gateway projection, and projected
  `sessions_history` boundary. The full affected files now pass:

  ```text
  server-methods.test.ts: 172 passed
  embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.test.ts: 40 passed
  sessions-history-tool.test.ts: 14 passed
  ```

  The sessions-history coverage includes raw image data, empty Base64 replacing
  stale byte metadata with `0`, and preservation of existing bytes when data is
  already omitted.

- Focused formatting and Oxlint pass. Production core types and core test types
  pass with the repository's `tsgo` runners.
