target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): add timeouts to model discovery requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Amazon Bedrock model discovery could wait indefinitely when the Bedrock control-plane model listing calls stalled, leaving setup and model catalog refresh paths without a bounded failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bedrock discovery now wraps both `ListFoundationModels` and paginated `ListInferenceProfiles` SDK calls in a local 30-second abort deadline using the AWS SDK `client.send(..., { abortSignal })` contract. The existing best-effort fallback remains unchanged: profile discovery failures still degrade to no profiles, and failed foundation discovery still returns an empty discovered catalog.

## User Impact

Users and operators get a bounded Bedrock model discovery failure instead of an indefinitely pending setup or catalog refresh when the AWS control plane stalls. Successful discovery behavior and cached catalog behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts` passed: 24 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude --model claude-fable-5 --thinking high` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Verified the installed AWS SDK/Smithy client type accepts `client.send(command, options)` and Smithy HTTP handler options include `abortSignal`.

### 2026-07-12 follow-up: exact-head local discovery timeout proof

- Exact PR head verified locally: `29b7aaff4eb2a5396ab4dd875a2b6e2e14935366`.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`.
- Result: passed 1 Vitest shard in 19.32s; 24 tests passed.
- Coverage from the focused file: Bedrock model/profile discovery timeout behavior, abort-aware discovery calls, and fallback completion for stalled discovery paths covered by the PR's local regression tests.
- This is controlled local provider-path proof only. No live AWS Bedrock API call was made, and no real AWS account, region, network stall, or Bedrock control-plane response was exercised.

## Proof

### 2026-07-12 exact-head local discovery tests after latest update-branch

- Exact head tested after normal `gh pr update-branch`: `0600633efef1c0fc30f7b4923066f99d75cd322a`.

- Not tested / remaining review gap: no real AWS Bedrock account, foundation-model discovery, inference-profile discovery, or AWS control-plane stall was exercised. This local proof should not be represented as the real-account proof ClawSweeper requested.
### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled AWS SDK transport proof

- Exact head: `e81f9f99e55ce2c5e29dc8230ab1b10cdd77a252`.
- Scope: controlled local Bedrock control-plane transport proof. This is not a live AWS account or Bedrock service run.

target.title: feat(cron): emit session.maintenance.pruned diagnostic event on reaper pruning
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105198

The session reaper (`sweepCronRunSessions`) only emits a text log when it prunes cron run sessions. No structured diagnostic event exists, making it impossible to monitor session-store maintenance health via OpenTelemetry or Prometheus.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Adds a `session.maintenance.pruned` trusted diagnostic event. Emitted only when `pruned > 0`. Carries only `pruned` (number) — no session keys, store paths, or unbounded identifiers. Follows the same pattern as existing `session.recovery.*` and `session.state` events.

Design:
- Trusted event → only visible to core-owned OTEL/Prometheus exporters
- Counter semantics: `counter.add(pruned)` per sweep → dashboards show cumulative pruned total

#### User Impact

No visible impact. Operators gain structured reaper throughput metrics.

#### Evidence

- **Type check / Lint:** `tsgo` + `oxlint` clean
- **Tests:** `session-reaper.test.ts` 22 tests (+2), OTEL 107, Prometheus 17 — no regressions

target.title: fix(twitch): time out Helix user resolution lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users resolving Twitch targets could wait indefinitely when Helix user lookup requests stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Twitch resolver now bounds Helix `getUserById` and `getUserByName` calls with the shared timeout helper while preserving the existing unresolved-target fallback path. The change is limited to user resolution and does not alter Twitch auth, delivery, or broader Twurple client setup.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

A stalled Twitch lookup now fails quickly enough for the resolver to return the existing not-resolved result instead of leaving setup or target resolution hanging.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/twitch/src/resolver.test.ts`
- Result: 1 test file passed, 2 tests passed.
- `git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD --`
- Result: passed.
## Proof

### 2026-07-13 exact-head controlled Twurple transport proof

- Exact PR head: `4f714316176c771441d2417db66f80106604dc35`.
- Scope: controlled local Helix transport through the production `resolveTwitchTargets()` entry point, the real Twurple `StaticAuthProvider`, and the real Twurple `ApiClient.users.getUserByName/getUserById` methods. Neither `@twurple/api` nor global fetch was mocked. This is not a live Twitch service outage.
- Harness: a temporary inline `node:http` server used Twurple 8.1.4's `TWURPLE_MOCK_API_PORT` transport hook. `/auth/validate` answered normally while selected `/mock/users` responses deliberately withheld headers. The harness was run from stdin and did not modify or commit repository files.
- Command:

  ```bash
  timeout 45s node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
  <temporary local Twurple transport harness>
  EOF
  ```

- Redacted username transcript:

  ```text
  proof: exact-head=4f714316176c controlled local Twurple Helix transport
  twurple-mock-api: http://localhost:<redacted-port>/mock/users
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver: normal-before result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser"}] elapsed=128ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=stall /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver-error: Failed to resolve @proofuser: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms
  resolver: stalled-username result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":false,"note":"API error: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms"}] elapsed=10007ms
  server: released /mock/users?login=proofuser after 9990ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?login=proofuser
  resolver: normal-after result=[{"input":"@proofuser","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser"}] elapsed=11ms
  ```

- Redacted user-ID transcript:

  ```text
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=stall /mock/users?id=4242
  resolver-error: Failed to resolve 4242: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms
  resolver: stalled-user-id result=[{"input":"4242","resolved":false,"note":"API error: Twitch Helix user lookup timed out after 10000ms"}] elapsed=10021ms
  server: released /mock/users?id=4242 after 9984ms
  server: accepted mode=normal /auth/validate
  server: accepted mode=normal /mock/users?id=4242
  resolver: normal-after result=[{"input":"4242","resolved":true,"id":"4242","name":"proofuser4242"}] elapsed=7ms
  ```

- Observation: both real Twurple lookup paths returned the existing unresolved result at the production 10-second budget. After the harness released each stalled response, a subsequent lookup through the same production entry point succeeded immediately, demonstrating resolver recovery.
- Not tested: live Twitch credentials, the public Twitch Helix service, proxy/TLS behavior, or a real provider outage. The caller-side timeout bounds OpenClaw's await but does not cancel Twurple's underlying fetch; the harness explicitly released each pending response after observing the fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord probe checks could hang after the `getMe` request returned response headers but the JSON response body stopped producing data.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord probe now reads the successful `getMe` JSON body through the bounded response reader with the existing 16 MiB cap and a per-chunk timeout tied to the probe timeout. Application metadata reads are also bounded, and the status entry point carries only the remaining caller timeout through cold lazy loading. Existing non-OK handling, malformed JSON wording, and the already-resolved bot result are preserved.

## User Impact

Discord configuration checks now return from stalled response bodies instead of waiting indefinitely. If optional application metadata stalls, the successful bot identity remains available.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3a470fcd81a815982a1669c4568518bb75551331`.

It used a real loopback `node:http` server and real Node `fetch`; the existing fetch seam only rewrote the fixed Discord origin to loopback while forwarding the production request options and abort signal. No mocked `Response`, Discord traffic, or credentials were used.


target.title: feat(ui): dismissible sidebar attention chips
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The sidebar attention chips (failing/overdue cron jobs, expired/expiring model auth) cannot be dismissed. A known-and-accepted problem — e.g. a cron job the user will fix later — nags on every page of every session with no way to snooze it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a small ✕ button to each chip. Dismissals are deliberately client-side chrome (like nav width or dock layout), stored per gateway in localStorage under `openclaw.control.sidebarAttention.v1:<gateway-scope>` — dismissing a nag on one device should not acknowledge it everywhere, and no new gateway state/RPC surface is warranted for a snooze.

A dismissal is signature-keyed, not forever: each chip carries a signature of the sorted entity ids behind it (cron job ids, provider ids). The chip stays hidden only while the exact same set is affected:

- a new job fails / a new provider expires → signature changes → chip resurfaces
- the state clears (jobs recover, auth refreshed) → the stale dismissal is pruned, so a later recurrence surfaces again
- expiring → expired is a different chip kind, so an escalation always resurfaces as an error

Pruning runs only against loaded data, so an empty pre-load snapshot can't wipe valid snoozes.

Dismissals are multi-tab safe: writes merge with the persisted map (read-modify-write) instead of a tab-held snapshot, and tabs listen for `storage` events, so a dismissal in one tab hides the chip in every tab of that browser without losing the other tab's entries.

## User Impact

Each attention chip now has a subtle ✕ (visible on the right, `common.dismiss` tooltip). Clicking it hides that chip on this browser/device for as long as the underlying state is unchanged. The navigate-on-click behavior of the chip body is unchanged.

![attention chips with dismiss](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-attention-dismiss/attention-dismiss-dark.png)

## Evidence

- `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention.ts`: chips gain `kind` + `signature`; chip markup restructured to sibling navigate/dismiss buttons (buttons can't nest).
- `ui/src/components/sidebar-attention-dismissals.ts`: the per-gateway load/save/prune dismissal store lives in its own module (keeps the exports prod-imported for the deadcode ratchet and the snooze logic pure/unit-testable).
- `ui/src/styles/layout.css`: pill container split into `__open` + `__dismiss` buttons; dismiss is muted, brightens on hover.
- Tests: `pnpm test ui/src/components/sidebar-attention.test.ts` — 7 passed (signature construction incl. sorted ids and disabled-job exclusion; `pruneDismissals` keep/resurface/clear cases).
- Live-verified in the mock Control UI harness (dark mode): dismissing the "Model auth expired: Gemini" chip hides it and writes `{"modelAuthExpired":"google"}` to the gateway-scoped key; reload keeps it hidden while the state is unchanged; planting stale signatures (`google\nopenai`, `stale-provider`) resurfaces both chips and prunes the stored map back to empty.
- Multi-tab live-verified with two browser tabs on the mock harness: tab B saw tab A's dismissal without reload (storage event), tab B's own dismissal merged with A's (both entries persisted), and tab A synced back to zero chips.
- Reuses the existing `common.dismiss` i18n key — no locale changes needed.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` previously read every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slipped through the binary heuristic could exhaust the process memory before the scan completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Replace the tracked-files scan with `git grep -n -z -o -I -E` so only exact conflict-marker matches are returned.
- Parse the grep output (path, line number, match) into violation records without buffering file contents.
- Keep `findConflictMarkersInFiles` for direct, small-scale use; the tracked-files path no longer reads files whole.
- `findConflictMarkersInTrackedFiles` now returns paths relative to the repository root, matching `git grep` output.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized or generated files can no longer cause an OOM during the scan because their contents are never read.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (9 tests) 585ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  9 passed (9)
```

Added regression tests covering:
- tracked files with conflict markers reported via `git grep`
- clean tracked files returning no violations
- binary tracked files skipped by `git grep -I`
- paths containing spaces and unusual characters
- large files whose line numbers are reported without reading the whole file
- `main()` printing paths relative to the repository root

Rebased onto current `upstream/main` to pick up the independent `scripts/lib/sqlite-reliability-runner.ts` async/await fix that was causing `check-test-types` and `checks-node-compact-small-2` failures.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cron jobs that deliver to a configured non-General Telegram forum topic could be marked delivered without Telegram proving the actual provider topic. If Telegram posted to General or another topic, cron delivery state could still look successful because it only had the intended route metadata and message result count.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram sends now surface provider-confirmed `chatId` / `messageThreadId` proof in `meta.telegram.messages[]`.

target.title: fix(node-pairing): require operator.admin to approve fs.listDir nodes (#105936)
target.body:
Closes #105936


## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators with only `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` scopes (without `operator.admin`) could approve a node surface that declares `fs.listDir`, even though invoking `fs.listDir` via `node.invoke` already correctly requires `operator.admin`. This is the same class of approval-versus-invoke scope mismatch previously fixed for `browser.proxy` in #104491.

## Why This Change Was Made

The approval-scope resolver in `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes` determines which operator scopes are required to approve a pending node pairing. It maintains an admin-level command list (`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`) that dictates which declared commands demand `operator.admin` at approval time. `fs.listDir` was added to the invoke-time admin gate in #105114 but was never included in the approval-time admin list, creating an asymmetry: the approval gate was weaker than the execution gate.

This change adds `NODE_FS_LIST_DIR_COMMAND` to `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS`, making the approval-time scope requirement match the existing invoke-time requirement. The approach is identical to the `browser.proxy` fix in #104491.

## User Impact

Operators with `operator.pairing` and `operator.write` can no longer approve a node pairing that declares `fs.listDir`. Such approvals now require `operator.admin`, consistent with the existing invoke-time authorization. Existing approved pairings are unaffected.

## Evidence

- **Unit test**: `resolveNodePairApprovalScopes(["fs.listDir"])` now returns `["operator.pairing", "operator.admin"]`

```
✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/node-pairing-authz.test.ts (6 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Integration test**: Full `node.pair.approve` RPC flow via gateway — 12 existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression to `system.run`, `browser.proxy`, or non-admin command approval paths.

```
✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server.node-pairing-authz.test.ts (12 tests)
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  12 passed (12)
```

- **Type check**: `tsgo:core` passes without errors.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: an `operator.write` (non-admin) operator can approve a node advertising the `fs.listDir` capability, whereas invoking `fs.listDir` requires `operator.admin`; the fix makes approval require `operator.admin` too.

Real environment tested: drove the real `approveNodePairing` reducer through its on-disk paired-device store in a fresh temp directory — the real `requestDevicePairing`, `approveDevicePairing`, `requestNodePairing`, `approveNodePairing`, and `resolveMissingRequestedScope` all ran against the real SQLite store, with nothing stubbed (the store was seeded through the real pairing request/approve functions).

Exact steps run after this patch: seed a paired node device, request a node surface declaring `commands: ["fs.listDir"]`, then call `approveNodePairing(requestId, { callerScopes: ["operator.pairing", "operator.write"] }, baseDir)` and record the returned outcome.

Evidence after fix:

```
caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.write]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> FORBIDDEN missingScope=operator.admin

caller scopes: [operator.pairing, operator.admin]
surface commands: [fs.listDir]
approveNodePairing -> APPROVED requestId=0795d316-6191-4d0c-ad8c-a723cb962e00
persisted commands: ["fs.listDir"]
```

## Reviewer Notes

Codex's review notes that the two admin-command classifications
(`ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` and `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS`) are
independently maintained, which has now caused two authorization mismatches
(#104491 for `browser.proxy`, this PR for `fs.listDir`).

This concern is well understood. However, the two lists are not identical by
design: `ADMIN_APPROVAL_COMMANDS` includes `system.run.*` (which requires
admin at approval time but not at invoke time, since `system.run` is already
protected by agent-layer `BLOCKED_INVOKE_COMMANDS` and descriptor-level scope
alignment), while `ADMIN_ONLY_NODE_INVOKE_COMMANDS` does not. A single shared
constant would either over-approximate one side or lose this semantic
distinction.

For this P1 security fix, I've kept the change minimal — the same pattern that
was merged for `browser.proxy` in #104491. Centralizing the admin-command
classification into a shared policy is a worthwhile follow-up refactor that
deserves more careful design consideration.

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using AI tools (opencode) with review by the author.

target.title: fix(recovery): reclaim terminal-phase reply operations in stuck-session recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stuck-session recovery unconditionally keeps the lane for any reply operation in the registry (`reason=active_reply_work`), even operations that will never produce progress — permanently wedging the lane until gateway restart.
- **Problem**: Two phantom scenarios exist:
  1. A ReplyOperation with terminal phase (completed/failed/aborted) remains in the registry via `retainFailureUntilComplete` or `terminalSettleTimer`. Recovery sees `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive = true` and keeps the lane forever — no progress data means `isActiveRunProgressStale` never triggers.
  2. A ReplyOperation in non-terminal phase (running) but with zero diagnostic progress events (`lastProgressAgeMs = undefined`). `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` for undefined ages, so the stale-progress path never fires. The lane stays wedged.
- **Solution**: 
  1. Terminal-phase check before `active_reply_work`/`keep_lane` — reclaim completed/failed/aborted operations after the 60s terminal settle window.
  2. `fallbackAgeMs` parameter in `isActiveRunProgressStale` — when no diagnostic progress exists, fall back to the overall session age so phantoms without any activity can still be reclaimed.
- **What changed**: `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts` (terminal-phase branch + `fallbackAgeMs` in stale check), `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` (settle window guard test, no-progress phantom test, `it.each` for all three terminal phases)
- **What did NOT change**: `reply-run-registry.ts`, `runs.ts`, `classifySessionAttention`, `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible`; deferred-maintenance and running-phase behavior; embedded run handle detection

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #105712
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Issue #105712 reports that a chat session lane can get wedged by a phantom active run: the lane's claim says an `embedded_run` is doing reply work, but no such run exists. The stuck-session recovery detects the stuck session, but then declines to act because `reason=active_reply_work` exempts the claim unconditionally. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.

This affects builds where a ReplyOperation finishes but stays in the registry (terminal phase) or where a run died before emitting any diagnostic events (no-progress phantom). The root cause is twofold:
1. `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined`
2. The reply-work branch has no fallback for terminal-phase operations

The diagnostic classification system (`classifySessionAttention`) also cannot set `allowActiveAbort: true` for these phantoms because there's no active work kind.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Session recovery keeps the lane for terminal-phase or no-progress reply operations, permanently wedging the channel lane until gateway restart
- Real environment tested: Linux (Ubuntu Azure VM), Node v24.14.0, branch `fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run tests that exercise the actual recovery function
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts
pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  31 passed (31)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)

$ pnpm test src/logging/diagnostic.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-run-registry.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  115 passed (115)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Terminal-phase reply operations (completed/failed/aborted, age > 60s settle window) are reclaimed — logged as "reclaiming terminal reply operation"
  2. Terminal-phase operations still within the 60s settle window keep the lane — logged as "still within settle window"
  3. No-progress phantoms (phase=running, no diagnostic activity, session age > 5 min) are reclaimed via `fallbackAgeMs` — logged as "reclaiming stale active reply work"
  4. Running-phase and queued-phase operations with active diagnostic progress keep the lane (unchanged)
  5. Deferred-maintenance operations keep the lane (unchanged)
  6. The `allowActiveAbort: true` recovery path is unaffected

- What was not tested:
  - Full gateway E2E with real Slack channel and phantom injection (requires long-running gateway and specific race conditions to reproduce)
  - The `terminalSettleTimer` path (60s settle window) is respected by the settle guard — if the timer fires normally the operation auto-clears before recovery sees it
  - macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

**Test evidence (post-rebase, Node v22.19.0)**:

Runtime tests — all 5 new tests pass:
```console
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=completed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=failed, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ reclaims terminal-phase reply operations (phase=aborted, phantom embedded_run) instead of keeping the lane
 ✓ keeps the lane when terminal-phase reply operation is still within the settle window
 ✓ reclaims no-progress reply operations (phase=running, phantom without diagnostic activity)
 ✓ (25 more pre-existing tests pass)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed | 1 failed (31)
```
The single failure (`logs stopped cron context when aborting an active embedded run`) is a pre-existing SQLite version issue (Node 22.19.0 embeds SQLite 3.50.4; OpenClaw requires 22.22.3+) — unrelated to this PR.

**E2E reclaim proof** — real gateway components + real `diag.warn()` terminal output:

```console
=== failed (retainFailureUntilComplete) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-failed sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s queueDepth=1 activeSessionId=e2e-failed-session phase=failed
stuck session recovery: sessionId=e2e-failed-session sessionKey=agent:main:e2e-failed age=61s action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true released=0
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted action=abort_embedded_run ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false released=0
→ Queued message: drained

=== aborted (running → abortByUser) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-aborted ... phase=aborted
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

=== completed (setPhase, no complete()) ===
stuck session recovery reclaiming terminal reply operation: sessionId=e2e-completed ... phase=completed
stuck session recovery: ... action=abort_embedded_run aborted=true drained=true
stuck session recovery outcome: status=aborted ... aborted=true drained=true forceCleared=false
→ Queued message: drained

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

The diagnostic warnings (`diag.warn()` calls inside `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession`) are captured directly and printed as terminal output — no mocks, no assertions-only. This is the exact log output that a running gateway produces when it reclaims a terminal-phase phantom.

**Additional real-runtime evidence**:
```
=== Gateway Dist Proof — Fix Code Verification ===
[1] recoverStuckDiagnosticSession loaded: OK ✓
[2] fallbackAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[3] terminalPhaseAgeMs in running dist: YES ✓
[4] Settle guard (6e4=60s): PRESENT ✓

=== Environment ===
Node: v22.22.2 (gateway process)
Branch: fix/reclaim-terminal-embedded-run-105712
Gateway health: {"ok":true,"status":"live"} (port 18789)

=== Test Results ===
runtime tests: 30/31 passed (1 pre-existing SQLite env failure)
integration tests: 10/10 passed (was 7)
Total: 40/41 passed across 2 suites
```

- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: No policy/permission surface touched
  - ✅ Enum completeness: All three terminal phases (`completed`/`failed`/`aborted`) covered via OR condition. No-diagnostic-progress phantom handled by `fallbackAgeMs` fallback (applies to any phase). Settle window (60s) prevents premature reclamation. `it.each` covers all three terminal phases + explicit settle window + no-progress tests.
  - ✅ Path coverage: Both call sites of `isActiveRunProgressStale` (active embedded run path and reply work path) pass `fallbackAgeMs`. The terminal-phase check is a new branch added before the existing `active_reply_work` return.
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: Both paths (terminal-phase reclaim and stale-progress reclaim) call the same `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun` function with `forceClear: true`. `clearState()` in `expireStaleReplyRunBySessionId` is idempotent (guarded by `stateCleared`).

## Root Cause

Two separate gaps in `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.ts`:

1. **Terminal-phase gap**: The `!activeSessionId && activeWorkSessionId && isEmbeddedAgentRunActive(...)` branch unconditionally returns `keep_lane` for any ReplyOperation still in the registry, even terminal-phase operations that have already completed/failed/aborted.

2. **No-progress gap**: `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when `lastProgressAgeMs` is `undefined` (no diagnostic events recorded). A phantom run that dies before first transcript flush leaves zero diagnostic activity, so the stale-progress path never fires. The session is permanently exempt from `keep_lane` → `active_reply_work`.

Both gaps interact: the diagnostic system sees no active work kind for these phantoms, so `classifySessionAttention` classifies them as `recoveryEligible` (correct) but `isActiveAbortRecoveryEligible` sees no `embedded_run` and never sets `allowActiveAbort: true`. The maintenance recovery path hits the `active_reply_work` gate and returns `keep_lane` — permanently.

## Regression Test Plan

| Target file | Scenario | What it protects |
|-------------|----------|-----------------|
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.runtime.test.ts` | phase=running + no handle → keep_lane | Active work not interrupted |
| (same) | phase=running + allowActiveAbort → abort | Stale abort path unchanged |
| (same) | phase=completed/failed/aborted + age > 60s → reclaim | **New**: Terminal zombies reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=completed + age < 60s settle window → keep_lane | **New**: Settle window respected |
| (same) | phase=running + no diagnostic activity + old session → reclaim | **New**: No-progress phantoms reclaimed |
| (same) | phase=deferred_maintenance → keep_lane | Deferred maintenance preserved |
| `diagnostic-stuck-session-recovery.integration.test.ts` | Full recovery flow | Recovery coordinator integration |
| `reply-run-registry.test.ts` | All registry operations | Registry lifecycle unaffected |

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None (fix to internal session recovery logic)

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: Unit tests for all three terminal phases + settle window guard + no-progress phantom + running + deferred-maintenance + stale-abort paths. 152 tests total across 4 suites.
- Edge cases checked: Non-terminal phases not reclaimed; settle window (< 60s) prevents premature reclaim; `undefined` phase handled safely by `else` fallthrough; empty diagnostic activity falls back to session age
- What you did NOT verify: Full gateway long-run with real phantom injection (requires production race conditions); macOS/Windows platforms (Linux only)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only changes behavior for terminal-phase operations and no-progress phantoms that were previously incorrectly kept alive
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The fix addresses both identified phantom scenarios (terminal-phase and no-progress) at the recovery decision point with minimal code change (one new `if` branch + `fallbackAgeMs` parameter). ClawSweeper's two P1 findings (phase-less phantom handling and terminal settlement guard) are both addressed.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Checking `isReplyRunEvidenceStale` in the recovery runtime — rejected because the recovery function doesn't directly access the operation object. (2) Narrowing `isEmbeddedAgentRunActive` in `runs.ts` — rejected because of broader usage across message queueing and abort paths. (3) Adding fallback to `classifySessionAttention` — rejected because the classification layer should stay focused on diagnostic activity, not reply-run-registry state.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Premature reclamation during the 60s terminal settle window, allowing follow-up turns to interleave with still-draining terminal delivery.

**Mitigation**: The settle guard checks `terminalPhaseAgeMs >= 60s` before reclaiming. In practice `stuckSessionWarnMs` (180s default) >> 60s settle window, so by the time recovery fires, the settle timer has long expired. The guard adds defense-in-depth for lower warn thresholds.

**Additional risk**: No-progress phantoms with `queueDepth = 0` (no queued messages) are still not reclaimed because `isActiveRunProgressStale` returns `false` when there's no work to process. This is by design — if no messages are queued, there's nothing to recover. Once a new message arrives, `queueDepth` becomes > 0 and recovery can proceed.

**Compatibility impact**: None.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users enabling bundled LSP servers with human-readable server keys could expose invalid or colliding agent tool names when those keys contain spaces, punctuation, numeric prefixes, or overlap with an existing registered tool name.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bundle LSP runtime now keeps the original server key for user-facing labels and execution details while deriving a provider-safe model-facing tool prefix for hover, definition, and references tools. The prefix is bounded to the existing 64-character tool-name budget and disambiguated against sibling LSP prefixes plus already registered tool names, matching the bundle MCP naming boundary without changing configuration, provider routing, or LSP protocol behavior.

## User Impact

Agents can use bundled LSP hover, definition, and references tools for readable server names such as `Type Script!` or numeric keys, and LSP tools are no longer dropped when the sanitized name would collide with a registered tool.

target.title: fix(line): drop blank entries from trailing commas in agenda/device directives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The LINE `[[agenda:]]` and `[[device:]]` directive parsers split their comma-separated lists without dropping blank entries. A trailing or doubled comma in agent output (common in LLM text) produces empty model entries:

- **agenda** → an empty-title event → an empty-string Flex `text` component. The LINE Messaging API rejects empty text with **HTTP 400**, so the whole agenda card is dropped and the user sees nothing.
- **device** → a control whose `label` is empty, which is likewise invalid.

The `[[quick_replies:]]` parser already avoids this by routing its split through the shared `normalizeStringEntries` helper (which trims and drops empties). Agenda and device did not, so a stray comma silently loses the message.

Fixes #105380

## Why This Change Was Made

Both parsers now route their comma-lists through the same `normalizeStringEntries` helper that `[[quick_replies:]]` uses, instead of an ad-hoc split. One canonical normalization path, no drift, and it matches the sibling directive that already got this right.

Scope note: `[[buttons:]]` is intentionally left out. Its blank-entry case is already handled on `main` by the `.filter((action) => action.label)` guard added in #105520 (which also drops blank-label actions like `:data`, a case the plain split would miss), so touching buttons here would be redundant and would regress that stronger check. This PR is scoped to the two directives that are still affected.

## User Impact

An agenda or device card with a trailing/doubled comma in the agent output now renders correctly instead of being dropped by LINE with an HTTP 400. No behavior change for well-formed input.

## Evidence

### 1. Real LINE API — the actual directive-generated payload

`parseLineDirectives("[[agenda: Today | Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]")` output posted to the LINE `validate/push` endpoint (validates a payload without sending; token/recipient redacted):

**Before (current `main`):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (3 events)
HTTP 400 - {"message":"A message (messages[0]) in the request body is invalid",
  "details":[{"message":"must be non-empty text",
  "property":"/body/contents/2/contents/2/contents/2/contents/0/text"}]}
```

**After (this PR):**
```
altText: 📋 Today (2 events)
HTTP 200 - {}
```

The 400 points at the empty `text` component deep inside the real agenda card; after the fix the generated payload validates.

### 2. Source-level reproduction (`parseLineDirectives`, current `main`)

| directive (trailing/doubled comma) | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[[agenda: Today \| Standup:9am, Lunch:12pm,]]` | 3 events, 1 empty `text` component | 2 events, 0 |
| `[[device: TV \| Box \| Playing \| Play:toggle,, Menu:menu]]` | 1 empty control label | 0 |

### 3. Tests

New regression tests in `reply-payload-transform.test.ts` (trailing-comma agenda, doubled-comma device). Verified red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
# without the fix (revert the two normalizeStringEntries calls):
 × drops trailing commas in agenda events
 × drops doubled commas in device controls
 Tests  2 failed | 18 passed (20)

# with the fix:
 Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and the extension typecheck are clean on the touched files.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inferred commitments could accept an impossible calendar date from model output. For example, `2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z` was normalized into May and could persist a check-in for a date the model never validly expressed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Due timestamps now use the existing strict absolute-time validation before retaining the original `Date.parse` result, preserving current timezone behavior. An invalid optional latest bound continues to use the existing 12-hour fallback instead of being normalized into another month.

This PR was AI-assisted. I reviewed the resulting code and tests and ran the repository's structured Codex autoreview.

Risk note: the change adds a single guard clause (`parseAbsoluteTimeMs(raw) !== null`) to an existing local helper `parseDueMs` in `src/commitments/extraction.ts:256`, reusing an established strict parser (`src/cron/parse.ts:65`) that shipped in v2026.6.9. The blast radius is limited to the inferred-commitment extraction pipeline; valid ISO timestamps, leap days, and explicit timezone offsets are preserved in the regression tests.

## User Impact

Users will no longer receive inferred commitment check-ins scheduled from calendar-invalid model timestamps. Valid leap-day and explicit timezone-offset timestamps continue to work as before.

target.title: fix(cli): stop stale session retry loops after failover
target.body:
Closes #97887

AI-assisted: implemented and reviewed with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CLI-backed turns could keep reusing an invalid session ID after a recoverable failover. Because the stale binding remained in session state, later turns could repeatedly resume the same broken CLI session instead of recovering with a fresh one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing CLI runner already supports a guarded fresh-session retry, but the direct reply and queued follow-up dispatch paths did not clear their stored binding before that retry. This change wires both paths to an atomic compare-and-clear helper. It clears only the expected stale CLI session across current memory and persistence, refuses to overwrite a newer concurrent binding, and does not recreate a session deleted during the failed attempt.

## User Impact

Users with Claude CLI or another CLI backend can recover from an expired or otherwise retryable stale session without entering a repeated failover loop. Concurrent session resets or replacements remain protected.

## Evidence

- Focused CLI dispatch suite: 23 passed.
- New queued follow-up recovery test: 1 passed with 149 unrelated tests skipped.
- Direct and queued-path combined suite: 276 passed; one existing thinking-level assertion also fails unchanged on origin/main.
- Follow-up full suite: 131 passed; 18 tests are blocked by the local Node 24.14 runtime because its embedded SQLite 3.51.2 is below the repository WAL-safety floor. The repository requires Node 24.15+ for this lane.
- oxfmt check passed for all changed files.
- oxlint passed for all changed files.

The added regression coverage verifies matching stale-state cleanup, protection of a newer persisted binding, missing-row lifecycle isolation, direct reply recovery, and queued follow-up recovery.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```

      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.

Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. target.title: fix(ios): typography audit rejects localized accessibility labels
target.body:
Related: #105859

AI-assisted: yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the iOS branded-typography test rejected localized accessibility labels that use SwiftUI `Text`, even though those labels are accessibility metadata and are not visually rendered. The Apple localization checker requires that typed form, leaving the two checks contradictory on current `main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The typography scanner now excludes `Text` calls used directly by `accessibilityLabel`, `accessibilityValue`, and `accessibilityHint`, including multiline formatting and nested localized constructors. A small Swift lexical mask plus balanced-parenthesis scan keeps strings/comments from influencing classification. Ordinary visual `Text` and `Label` calls remain subject to the branded-font audit, including when they share a line with accessibility metadata.

## User Impact

No runtime UI behavior changes. Maintainers can keep localized VoiceOver labels in their canonical SwiftUI form without making the typography test fail or weakening visual typography coverage.

## Evidence

- Before-fix scanner reproduction: `SettingsProTabSections.swift:877` and `SettingsProTabSections.swift:1403` reported as unbranded offenders.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in exec resume
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a child process spawned by `codex exec resume` could crash the runtime if its stdout or stderr pipe breaks (e.g., the process terminates abruptly before the pipe is drained). Stream-level `error` events on `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` were not handled — only the `child.on("error")` event was caught, which does not cover stream-level errors.

## Why This Change Was Made

The codex exec resume handler collects child process output via `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")`. These `Readable` streams can emit `error` independently from the child process itself when the pipe is destroyed before fully consumed. Node.js will throw an unhandled `error` event unless a listener is registered, which can crash the host process.

The fix adds no-op error handlers to both streams. Child-process-level errors are already handled by `child.on("error", reject)` on line 299, so stream errors can be safely ignored — the collected output (stdout/stderr buffers) will be incomplete, but the exit code and error path already handle that case.

## User Impact

Prevents a potential process crash when the codex CLI child process terminates abnormally during an exec resume operation. No behavioral change for normal operation.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `78083c4e03`

**Real behavior proof — stream error does not crash the process:**

The following terminal output demonstrates that when the stdout pipe is destroyed (simulating a broken pipe), the registered error handler catches the error and the host process survives:

```
[proof] stdout error caught (expected, not crashing)
[proof] child exit code: 1
[proof] stdout collected: (empty due to destroyed pipe)
[proof] SUCCESS: process survived stdout stream error without crashing
```

Reproduce: `node -e '<script that spawns a child and destroys stdout>'`

**Focused regression tests — 9/9 passed (6 existing + 3 new stream-error tests):**

```

 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > lists sessions from Codex session files... 9ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > reports malformed node session payloadJSON... 6ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > keeps Codex history session previews... 4ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex cli node sessions > keeps Codex session-file previews... 5ms
 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > survives stdout stream errors without crashing... 72ms

 ✓ |extension-codex| node-cli-sessions.test.ts > codex exec resume stream error handling > survives both stdout and stderr errors simultaneously... 80ms

      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**Diff:**

-    child.stdout.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stdout.push(chunk));
-    child.stderr.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stderr.push(chunk));
+    child.stdout.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => stdout.push(chunk)).on("error", () => {});

target.title: fix(agents): terminate agent run on critical loop detection instead of continuing indefinitely
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When loop detection blocks a tool at critical level (e.g., `generic_repeat` detector, `action=block`, `count=10`), the tool result with `deniedReason: "tool-loop"` was returned to the model normally. The model kept retrying the same tool, and the session continued burning resources for hours (logs show 2.8h of repeated blocked messages after the first critical block).

Fixes #106231.

## Changes

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` (toolSearchCatalogExecutor):
  After `runToolLifecycle` returns a tool result, check if `details.deniedReason === "tool-loop"`.
  If so, call `abortRun()` to terminate the agent run.
- The current turn's blocked result still reaches the model, but `abortRun()` sets `aborted=true`
  and triggers `runAbortController.abort()`, causing `isStopped()` to return true and
  cancelling any subsequent provider requests.

## Evidence

**Flow verification:**

Before:
```
result (deniedReason=tool-loop) → return result → model retries same tool → ∞ loop
```

After:
```
result (deniedReason=tool-loop) → abortRun() → aborted=true
→ runAbortController.abort() → isStopped()=true → provider cancelled → run terminates
```

```
=== Before (bug) ===
attempt.ts had NO check for deniedReason === 'tool-loop':
  result → return result → model retries → INFINITE LOOP

=== After (fix) ===
attempt.ts:3711-3717 checks deniedReason === 'tool-loop':
  → abortRun() → aborted=true
  → runAbortController.abort()
  → isStopped()=true → no more model turns
  → provider cancelled → run terminated

=== Abort Chain ===
abortRun(false, error):
  → aborted = true
  → runAbortController.abort(error)
    → runAbortController.signal.aborted = true
    → all abort event listeners fire
    → provider requests cancelled
    → next steer message rejected (isStopped=true)
    → agent run terminates cleanly
```

target.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users in external chats such as WhatsApp could see automatic runtime notices when model fallback, usage limits, compaction, backend failures, heartbeat checks, ACP status, plugin-binding failures, or tool/progress warnings happened.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped update this branch and evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `messages.operationalReplies` so operators can control automatic operational notices separately from normal assistant replies. The policy supports `always`, `silent`, `once`, and `redirect`; `redirect` writes notices to an operator session through `redirectSessionKey`, and `sendPolicy: deny` still wins.

The policy is applied across direct dispatch, ACP delivery, ACP status projection, queued follow-ups, compaction notices, route-failure notices, heartbeat delivery, progress/status callbacks, plugin-binding notices, tool warnings, and block/final replies. Normal message-tool replies, authorized command replies, before-run block replies, and background ACP child suppression keep their existing behavior.

Redirect-failure behavior uses the maintainer-selected fail-closed contract: if the configured operator redirect write fails, the source chat remains suppressed and the failure is logged instead of exposing operational details back to the source chat.

A follow-up review found plain `isError` payloads were too broad to classify as operational notices. This branch now treats only explicit notice flags or internal notice metadata as operational, and it keeps normal error replies visible under `messages.operationalReplies`.

target.title: fix(cron): batch pending-media snapshot in session reaper to avoid O(SxT) loop
target.body:
#### What Problem This Solves

Close #105694

Fixes an O(S × T) CPU bottleneck in the cron session reaper that blocks the Node.js event loop on each timer tick. For every cron continuation row, `sweepCronRunSessions` called `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey`, which internally performs a full cloned-and-sorted task-registry snapshot via `listTaskRecords`. With thousands of sessions, this synchronous work saturates the main thread and causes gateway timeout / WebSocket disconnection.

#### Why This Change Was Made

Instead of changing the per-row `hasPendingGeneratedMediaTaskForSessionKey` helper (still used by the single-invocation `cron-run-continuation-cleanup` path), this adds `buildPendingGeneratedMediaSessionKeySet` — a one-shot snapshot that collects all session keys with pending generated-media work by iterating the in-process activity map once and the full task registry once. The reaper then does O(1) `Set.has()` lookups inside the loop.

Key design decisions:
- Preserves the exact `requesterSessionKey` / `ownerKey` matching contract — no semantic change, only a scan-lifting optimization
- The snapshot is deliberately conservative: session keys that the reaper never visits may still be included, which is harmless

#### User Impact

No visible impact. The cron reaper produces identical pruning decisions with strictly less CPU time per sweep.

#### Evidence

- **Type check:** `tsgo` passes with no errors
- **Unit tests:**
  - `task-status-access.test.ts` — 10 tests pass (+6)
  - `session-reaper.test.ts` — 20 tests pass
  - `cron-run-continuation-cleanup.test.ts` — 5 tests pass (no regression)
- **Change scope:** 5 files, +131 −7 lines. No config, CLI, SDK, docs, or changelog surface.
- **No new dependencies**
- **Real gateway startup + 6-minute run + clean shutdown** (Node v22.23.1, 11 production plugins):

```

[gateway] agent model: vendor/model-name (thinking=off, fast=off)

[gateway] starting channels and sidecars...
[matrix] [default] starting provider (http://10.x.x.x:xxxxx)
[plugins] embedded acpx runtime backend registered lazily
[gateway] ready
[gateway] agent runtime plugins pre-warmed in 211ms

  … 6+ minutes stable runtime, cron timer ticks fire cleanly …

[gateway] signal SIGTERM received
[gateway] received SIGTERM; shutting down
[shutdown] started: gateway stopping
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 1052ms
```

- **No reaper errors or warnings** over a full cron-timer cycle (6+ minutes). The gateway starts, runs, and shuts down identically to main — the only difference is strictly less CPU time per reaper sweep.
- **Gateway-proof (vi.spyOn only, real production modules):** exercised `sweepCronRunSessions` with `vi.spyOn` on `listTaskRecords`. Tasks seeded through real `createTaskRecord` → real SQLite persistence.

```

  old path would have called listTaskRecords ~25 times (per continuation row)

  [correctness] old vs new: 50/50 match, 0 mismatch
  pending set size: 33

  [perf] S=100, T=200, listTaskRecords calls: 1, sweep: 34.45ms
  [perf] old path would call listTaskRecords ~50 times

 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  4 passed (4)
```

- **`listTaskRecords` called exactly 1x per sweep** at S=50 and S=100 (old path: ~S/2 times)
- **50/50 decisions match** between old per-row helper and new one-shot snapshot
- **Contract preserved**: requester + owner session keys both captured; terminal tasks excluded; chat/non-media ignored

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; provisioning rows are leases with heartbeats (`lastActiveAt` bumped at claim, post-copy, and at the ready flip): gc reaps only leases SILENT past `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — a persisted holder-liveness signal, so claim age alone can never kill a live-but-slow holder — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`; a provisioning row whose directory vanished is hard-deleted (branch + row; no snapshot, no user work) so the name stays genuinely retriable). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103239
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `create()` performs the irreversible git-side effects (`git worktree add`, branch creation) before the registry insert, with no crash-window reconciliation: `reconcileOrphans()` treated "git still lists this directory as a live worktree" purely as a preserve signal and never checked whether the worktree matches the managed naming scheme but lacks a registry row.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no adopt-or-repair path for the crashed-create signature; `create()`'s branch-exists guard had no way to distinguish "user's foreign branch" from "our own crashed create()".
- Contributing context (if known): the registry has no `name` column (name derives from the path's last segment), so adoption needs no extra bookkeeping — the orphan is fully re-derivable from path + branch.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [ ] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/worktrees/service.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a live worktree + managed branch with no registry row (the exact end-state of a crash between `git worktree add` and the registry insert) is adopted by a retried `create()` with the same name — preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId`, re-running provisioning (include files + setup script restored, real `baseRef` recorded), and holding the loser-touches-nothing / holder-only-destruction invariants under deterministic interleavings; gc during an in-flight normal `create()` adopts nothing and exactly one live row remains; a parked in-flight create cannot be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name retry (same-owner and foreign-owner both covered, setup executes exactly once); a failing setup leaves no worktree, branch, or registry row.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the tests use the real `git` binary and real SQLite registry (the file's established pattern — no mocks), produce the crash end-state via production code (`create()` then deleting only the registry row), and assert through the public service API only.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): "deletes unregistered orphan debris but preserves git-listed worktrees" covers the foreign/detached case and stays green, locking in that non-managed worktrees are never claimed.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- A retried `create()` with the same name after a crashed create now succeeds (adopts, re-provisions, returns the record) instead of failing with `branch already exists`.
- gc behavior is unchanged from upstream (preserve-only for live worktrees); foreign or detached-HEAD worktrees are unaffected.
- Concurrent same-path registrations can no longer produce duplicate live registry rows (atomic claim; loser gets the existing "name already in use" semantics).
- `list()` now shows a worktree from claim-time (during provisioning) rather than after setup completes; failed creates still end with no registry row.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
create() crash after `git worktree add` -> live worktree + branch, no registry row
  -> create(same name): "branch already exists" (dead end; manual git surgery required)
```

target.title: fix(agents): provide actionable recovery guidance on context overflow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users whose agent runs exec commands producing large output (e.g. `kubectl logs`, `cat` of large files) would see only "The agent run failed before producing a reply." — an opaque dead-end message with no recovery path — when the tool result causes unrecoverable context overflow.

The session enters `livenessState: "blocked"` but the user is never told what happened, why, or how to recover.

Related issue: #106204

## Why This Change Was Made

Improved all three user-facing error messages in the overflow/failure path to include concrete recovery commands (`/compact`, `/new`) and a practical tip about re-running commands with tighter output filters:

- `run.ts` `overflowRecoveryText`: replaced generic message with structured recovery options
- `agent-runner-execution.ts` `preserveSessionMapping` path: appended tool output tip
- `chat-display-projection.ts` `GATEWAY_ASSISTANT_ERROR_FALLBACK_TEXT`: added `/compact` and `/new` hints

This is a display-layer-only change — no modification to core recovery logic.

## User Impact

Users hitting context overflow now see actionable guidance instead of a dead-end error. They can immediately try `/compact` or `/new` without needing to search docs or ask for help.

## Evidence

- `npx oxlint@1.72.0` on all 3 modified source files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `npx vitest run server-methods.test.ts`: 170/171 tests pass (1 failure is pre-existing SQLite version check unrelated to this change)
- No logic changes — purely string constant modifications
